sheet-1.description: Sheet 1, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the northern edge of downtown Elizabeth west of North Broad Street, between Prince Street at the top and Westfield Avenue at the bottom, with the Elizabeth River curving down the left side of the sheet. Union Avenue runs straight down the middle of the sheet from Prince Street to Morris Avenue, and Westminster Avenue and North Broad Street form the right edge. Irvington Avenue and Irvington Place cut the upper left corner. The upper half is a district of large residential lots with frame and brick dwellings, many of them still deep and open behind the houses; Public School No. 10 stands on Prince Street west of Union Avenue, the Westminster Presbyterian Church occupies the corner of Prince Street and Westminster Avenue, and a Knights of Columbus club house stands on Union Avenue. The lower half is more commercial. Morris Avenue crosses the river on a stone bridge and runs south-east to Westfield Avenue, lined with brick stores and dwellings. The block between Union Avenue, Morris Avenue and North Broad Street holds the large Hersh Bros. Ford sales and service garage, auto repair and refinishing shops, a service station and machine shop, and The Elks Club, with the fire-proof U.S. Post Office facing North Broad Street. Garages, a welding shop and dwellings line Mulberry Street near Westfield Avenue. A 24-inch water main from the reservoir to the pumps crosses the open riverside ground at the left. The ground south of Westfield Avenue, around Union Street and Harrison Street, is left blank; it is drawn on sheet 3. The left margin is marked 'See Volume Two'.
notes: Public School No. 10 stands on Prince Street west of Union Avenue.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, covers the ground east of North Broad Street on the northern edge of downtown Elizabeth, between North Broad Street and Westminster Avenue at the top, Magnolia Avenue at the right, and East Broad Street and Walnut Street at the bottom. The four-track main line of the Pennsylvania Railroad crosses the middle of the sheet on an embankment, carried over Chestnut Street and Magnolia Avenue on stone arches, with a street railway car yard beside it north of the tracks. Above the railroad, Trinity Episcopal Church and its chapel stand on Chestnut Street at North Broad Street; North Broad Street is lined with brick stores, a Public Service Corporation office, an auto accessories store and offices; and two large garages, for 25 and 70 cars, stand at the corner of North Broad Street and Magnolia Avenue. Trinity Place is a short street of frame dwellings between Chestnut Street and Magnolia Avenue. Below the railroad, the yard of The Anchor Construction Co. with storage, a cement block factory and contractors' supply sheds fills the block between Chestnut and Magnolia, and frame dwellings, warehouses, a plumber, a mission hall, a carpenter shop, a Chinese laundry, second-hand lumber sheds and a vulcanizing shop line Chestnut Street, Walnut Street and East Broad Street. Westfield Avenue enters at the upper left and Prince Street at the upper right corner. The upper left, the wide street ground of North Broad Street, and the lower right corner (drawn on sheet 6) are largely blank.
notes: The Pennsylvania Railroad main line crosses Chestnut Street and Magnolia Avenue on stone arches.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the heart of downtown Elizabeth around the Central Railroad of New Jersey station, between Westfield Avenue at the top and West Grand Street at the bottom, and from the Elizabeth River on the left to North Broad Street and Broad Street on the right. Morris Avenue runs diagonally from Westfield Avenue down to the railroad, lined on both sides with brick stores, the Bellview Hotel, restaurants, barbers, an auto service station, upholsterer, picture framer and offices. The block between Westfield Avenue, Harrison Street and Union Street holds a large raised garage for 125 cars, other garages, auto repair and show rooms, a blacksmith shop and a wholesale grocery; frame dwellings line Harrison Street, Union Street and Crane Street below it, and Julian Place has a row of brick stores with an express office and plumber. Garages for 75 and 20 cars, battery service shops and a wall paper and painting store stand on Westfield Avenue and North Broad Street. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet on its own right-of-way, with the West Bound and East Bound passenger stations, a clock tower and a subway between the platforms, an iron bridge over Union Street and a steel bridge over the Elizabeth River. The Pennsylvania Railroad crosses it diagonally at the lower right on stone arches over Broad Street and a skew iron bridge, with its own West Bound and East Bound passenger stations. South of the railroads are the Mulford Coal and Lumber Co. yard with a coal trestle and lumber sheds, Banner Bros. fancy leather goods factory, dwellings, a photo developing and printing works, and the Dix Building on Broad Street. Stone bridges carry Crane Street and West Grand Street over the river. The ground south of West Grand Street is left blank (sheet 7).
notes: Central Railroad of New Jersey Elizabeth station: West Bound and East Bound passenger stations with a subway between them and a clock tower.
Pennsylvania Railroad West Bound and East Bound passenger stations stand at the lower right, where the line crosses Broad Street on stone arches.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the east side of Broad Street in downtown Elizabeth, from East Broad Street at the top down to East Jersey Street and Hampton Place at the bottom, and east to Jefferson Avenue. The upper half is taken up by the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard, with the C.R.R. of N.J. freight station and platforms, an iron bridge carrying the line over Broad Street, and the Pennsylvania Railroad crossing the upper left corner on stone arches. Along East Broad Street on the north side of the yard stand the refrigerator houses of Swift and Co., Morris and Co. and Armour and Co., a smoke house, a florist and green house, a Western Union Telegraph Co. warehouse and the Enterprise Coal and Supply Co. lime and cement storage; a gas holder stands at the upper right. The Hall and Carlton coal and wood yard with a trestle and the Hersh & Bro. grocery warehouse lie on the south side of the yard. Between Broad Street, the railroad and Price Alley are The Elizabeth Evening Times printing office and press room, the Hotel Whittman, the L. F. Hersh & Bro. wholesale grocery, the New York Telephone Co. exchange and Fire Department Engine Co. No. 2. East Grand Street has stores, a woodworking shop, the National Wood Staining Co., a Chinese laundry, a Veteran Firemen's Association hall and rows of frame dwellings; south of it are the new New York Telephone Co. building (built 1919), the Elizabeth Hardware Co., Laggren Bros. tent and awning factory, a clothing factory, a bank, restaurants and stores on Broad Street, and the Second Presbyterian Church on East Jersey Street. Drake Alley runs diagonally between East Grand Street and East Jersey Street, parallel to Jefferson Avenue, lined with brick and frame dwellings.
notes: Price Alley is the southern leg of the modern Commerce Place (Commerce Place in the reference data); it is drawn 35 ft wide.
Drake Alley has no street of that name in the modern reference data.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, covers a thinly built residential district north of downtown Elizabeth, between North Broad Street on the left and Walnut Street on the right, from Whitehead Place at the top down to Magnolia Avenue at the bottom. The four tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad run straight down the middle of the sheet, crossing Mary Street on an iron bridge. Pennsylvania Avenue and Trinity Place run parallel to the railroad on its west side, and Mary Street crosses the sheet diagonally from North Broad Street to Walnut Street. Prince Street enters at the lower left corner, where it meets North Broad Street and Magnolia Avenue, and Anna Street leaves Walnut Street to the east. Most lots are large and many are empty. Frame dwellings stand along North Broad Street, Pennsylvania Avenue, Trinity Place and Walnut Street, with a few brick-veneered houses on North Broad Street, a carpenter shop off Pennsylvania Avenue, and a garage for 40 cars with buried gasoline tanks at the corner of North Broad Street and Mary Street. The largest building is the Armory of the New Jersey National Guard on Magnolia Avenue at Walnut Street, a brick drill hall with National Guard offices along its Magnolia Avenue front and Gamewell auxiliary fire alarm boxes. The big block between the railroad and Walnut Street is mostly open ground. A compass rose and the scale bar fill the open margin at the left; the ground beyond the sheet edges is drawn on neighbouring sheets.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, covers a residential district north-east of downtown Elizabeth, from Walnut Street on the left to Madison Avenue on the right and from Anna Street at the top down to Chestnut Street at the bottom. Linden Street and Jefferson Avenue cross the sheet from top to bottom, Magnolia Avenue crosses it from side to side, and East Broad Street cuts diagonally through the lower middle from Chestnut Street to Magnolia Avenue. Most of the four large blocks are filled with two- and three-storey frame dwellings, with a few brick houses, private garages, sheds and a carpenter shop; a plumber has a shop on Jefferson Avenue. Industry and trade concentrate in the lower left block between Walnut Street, Linden Street, Magnolia Avenue and Chestnut Street: the American Railway Express Co. and Alderney Dairy Co. stables and wagon house, a hay store, lumber storage and the Fischer & Dackerman auto and wagon works with a wood working shop, blacksmith and paint shop and buried gasoline tanks. In the lower right block between Jefferson and Madison Avenues stand the Elizabeth Awning Co., a concrete block garage for 50 cars with buried gasoline tanks, and stores. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the lower right corner on an iron bridge. The ground above Anna Street (sheet 77) and below Chestnut Street (sheets 2 and 9) is left blank. A compass rose stands in the open ground at the upper left.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the business centre of Elizabeth on the west side of Broad Street, from West Grand Street at the top down to Caldwell Place at the bottom and from Price Street, at the edge of the Elizabeth River, east to Broad Street. The Pennsylvania Railroad main line crosses the sheet diagonally on an embankment, carried over West Grand Street and West Jersey Street on stone arches, with its freight station, projection and platform beside Sterling Place. West of the railroad, the blocks along Price Street and Union Street hold rows of frame dwellings, a paints and oils store and an office; a stone bridge carries West Grand Street over the river at the upper left. East of the railroad the Broad Street frontage is the city's main shopping street: the Union County Trust Company (fire-proof, built 1909), the Western Union office, Woolworth's 5 and 10 cent store, Woodhull's department store, the Masonic Hall and Masonic Lodge, and the Goerke-Kirch Co. department store in a fire-proof reinforced concrete building of 1922. South of West Jersey Street are the S. H. Kress & Co. 5 and 10 cent store, the Morey La Rue Laundry Co. works with its wagon house and water tank, the Elizabeth Journal office with composing, stereotype and press rooms, the National State Bank (fire-proof, built 1920), a hardware store, a bank and stores. The Union Garage for 70 cars and a blacksmith stand on Union Street, Union Place is a short street of 27 ft, and Caldwell Place has a row of brick and frame dwellings. Murray Street enters at the lower left. A compass rose stands in the open block between Sterling Place and the river.
notes: Union Street south of West Jersey Street is now Elizabethtown Plaza; its junction with West Jersey Street lies about 4 m from the modern node and was not used as control.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the business district on the east side of Broad Street south of East Jersey Street, between Broad Street on the left, East Jersey Street at the top, West Scott Place on the right and Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom. Jefferson Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, Washington Street crosses it from Broad Street to West Scott Place, and Osborn Place is a short court of frame dwellings east of Jefferson Avenue. Broad Street and East Jersey Street are lined with brick stores and offices; the Y.M.C.A., large furniture stores and stock rooms, a bakery and Proctor's Theatre with its stage and dressing rooms fill the East Jersey Street frontage. Further down Broad Street are the Capitol Motion Picture Theatre (fire-proof, built 1913), the Regent Theatre (fire-proof construction), and a motion picture theatre being dismantled; William Fox's Liberty Theatre (fire-proof, built 1913) stands on Elizabeth Avenue. St. John's Episcopal Church with its tower, Sunday school rooms and rectory stand behind the Broad Street stores, the Third Presbyterian Church with chapel and Sunday school faces East Jersey Street, and the Siloam Presbyterian Church, a mission hall and the L.O.O.M. Moose Home stand on Washington Street. Industry is represented by the Superior Novelty Mfg. Co., makers of celluloid and metal novelties, with its celluloid storage, the D. & D. Machine & Tool Co. machine shop, the William McCormack livery, a 15-car garage and a stove ware house. Elizabeth Avenue is lined with stores, upholsterers, an undertaker and a photographer. Rahway Avenue enters at the lower left corner. The ground above East Jersey Street belongs to sheets 4 and 9.
notes: Washington Street is now Dickinson Street (OpenStreetMap).
West Scott Place is now Winfield Scott Plaza (OpenStreetMap).
Osborn Place has no counterpart in the modern reference data.

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 9, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, covers the ground east of Broad Street between the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Hampton Place, from East Broad Street and Chestnut Street at the top to Madison Avenue at the right, with Jefferson Avenue running down the middle. The upper half is taken up by the Central Railroad of New Jersey: its main line crosses Madison Avenue on an iron bridge, and a fan of yard tracks spreads out towards the C.R.R. of N.J. freight yard on sheet 4. Beside the tracks are the John Knight coal yard on East Broad Street, the Wilson & Co. meat house and a round storage building for railroad supplies on Chestnut Street, the J. P. Brophy coal yard with a long coal shed, and the J. & S. S. Thompson coal and wood yard with bins, an elevator, a machine shop and a carpenter shop. East Grand Street crosses the sheet diagonally, lined with frame dwellings, a row of brick stores, a bakery with ovens, a Chinese laundry and a small pants factory. The block south of East Grand Street holds the Jr. O.U.A.M. hall and the Joseph Freedman wholesale grocery with its furniture warehouse and grocery storage; the rest of the block between Jefferson Avenue, Madison Avenue and Hampton Place is filled with frame dwellings, including the American Home Association. William Street and Lafayette Street meet Madison Avenue at the right edge. A compass rose stands in the open ground above the inset; the lower left corner of the sheet is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: J. & S. S. Thompson coal and wood yard and J. P. Brophy coal yard lie beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey.
Joseph Freedman wholesale grocery and the Jr. O.U.A.M. hall stand on Jefferson Avenue south of East Grand Street.

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 9 is a boxed inset in the lower left corner, cut off from the main map by a heavy line, drawn at the same scale of 50 ft to an inch and the same orientation. It shows the single block between Hampton Place at the top and East Jersey Street at the bottom, from Jefferson Avenue at the left to Madison Avenue at the right, a block that falls between the main map of this sheet and sheet 8 below it. Hampton Place is lined with a row of two-storey frame and brick dwellings numbered 1108 to 1130, with a chiropodist's office at the Jefferson Avenue corner and a small carpenter shop behind them. The East Jersey Street frontage holds the Central Baptist Church, with three towers, a Y.W.C.A. building, and brick stores occupied by an undertaker, a barber and a tailor at the Jefferson Avenue corner. A few large frame dwellings and a concrete-block auto house stand on Madison Avenue. Water pipes are marked along Hampton Place, Jefferson Avenue and East Jersey Street. Below the inset the ground is left for sheet 8 (with West Scott Place and Jefferson Avenue lettered at its edge); the street widths printed are 50 ft for Hampton Place, 60 ft for Jefferson Avenue, 66 ft for Madison Avenue and 70 ft for East Jersey Street.

sheet-10.description: Residential blocks in central Elizabeth east of Broad Street, bounded by East Grand Street on the north, Catherine Street on the east, East Jersey Street on the south and Madison Avenue on the west, crossed by William Street and Lafayette Street. Hampton Place enters Madison Avenue from the west, and Elizabeth Street leaves Catherine Street to the east. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The two northern blocks are lined with closely spaced two- and three-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few brick-veneered houses and stores at the Catherine Street corners. On East Grand Street stand the Union Baptist Church at the Madison Avenue corner and the brick machine shop of Row and Davis Engineers Inc. (Paracoil Specialties), with welding, riveting and stock rooms. The large southern block between Lafayette and East Jersey Streets is more open: its centre is taken by the brick Winfield Scott School with its auditorium and boiler room, and it also holds the Home for Aged Women on East Jersey Street, a row of six brick dwellings, the B and B Carpet Cleaning Works and the E. H. Miller upholstery shop off Catherine Street, storage buildings and many automobile garages behind the houses. Water pipes of 4 to 20 inches are drawn in the streets, with fire alarm boxes at the corners. At the foot of the sheet, south of East Jersey Street, the edge of a small park between West and East Scott Places is shown; Morrel Street is marked to the south-east. Only the street lines of the neighbouring blocks across Madison Avenue and Catherine Street are drawn, as they belong to sheets 9 and 17.

sheet-11.description: Blocks in central Elizabeth north of East Grand Street, bounded by Anna Street on the north, Catherine Street on the east, East Grand Street on the south and Madison Avenue on the west, crossed by Bond Street, Magnolia Avenue and the main line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey. Meadow Street runs diagonally from Magnolia Avenue north-east to Monroe Avenue and Anna Street, cutting off a triangular block of small dwellings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. North of the railroad the blocks hold two- and three-storey frame dwellings and flats, with an undertaker, a painter, an auto painting shop, a Chinese laundry, a pressing and cleaning shop and a plumber among them. South of Magnolia Avenue the W. J. Boehm woodworking mill and lumber yard backs onto the railroad with its sheds and lumber piles, beside a warehouse and sash storage. The railroad crosses the sheet in a wide band of tracks with a coal trestle, carried over Madison Avenue and Catherine Street on iron bridges. South of the tracks are large industrial plants: the Consumers Ice and Cold Storage Co. with its engine room, tank house, delivery room and cold storage, the Braunsdorf-Mueller Co. makers of steel tools with machine and forge shops, and the Elizabeth Lumber Co. yard; Blackstone Alley runs in from Catherine Street. A row of dwellings and stores lines East Grand Street at the foot of the sheet. Chestnut Street enters Madison Avenue from the west at the railroad bridge.

sheet-12.description: Blocks in central Elizabeth between Catherine Street on the west and Spring Street on the east, from Anna Street at the top of the sheet to East Grand Street at the foot, crossed by Bond Street, Magnolia Avenue and the main line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey. Oak Street runs south from Magnolia Avenue and passes under the railroad in a subway to East Grand Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The two northern blocks, between Anna Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue, are closely built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and stores, with a bake house, a paint shop, wagon sheds and private garages in the yards. The railroad crosses the middle of the sheet as a band of tracks carried over Catherine Street and Spring Street on iron bridges; beside it stand the C.R.R. of N.J. passenger station and a passenger shed, with a coal trestle at the west end. South of the tracks are the J. M. Rueter coal yard, a hollow-tile building for the storage of hay, grain and feed, and the brick foundation of a building destroyed by fire, then rows of dwellings and a few brick stores facing East Grand Street. Broadway leaves Spring Street to the east just south of the railroad. Blackstone Alley is lettered on the sheet 11 side of Catherine Street. The ground east of Spring Street and west of Catherine Street is left blank except for street lines, as it belongs to sheets 19 and 11.

sheet-13-1.description: The main part of sheet 13 covers the civic centre of Elizabeth west of Broad Street, south of the Elizabeth River and the Pennsylvania Railroad embankment. It is bounded by South Broad Street and Broad Street at the foot of the sheet, Caldwell Place on the east, and the river and the railroad on the north and west. Rahway Avenue runs north from Broad Street across the river on a stone bridge, and Union Street runs east from Rahway Avenue to Caldwell Place. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with north towards the right. The largest block holds the Union County Court House, with its 100-foot dome and fire-proof construction, the County Jail behind it, and the First Presbyterian Church with its parish house in the old burying ground. On Broad Street near the river stand the Free Public Library (fire-proof, built 1911) and a storage warehouse. Rahway Avenue is lined with dwellings, the Young Men's Catholic Association, a G.U.O. of O.F. hall, a jeweller and battery service and a large garage, with buried gasoline tanks. On Union Street are the Elizabeth Cornice Works Inc., an auto wrecking yard, a junk yard, the Mt. Teman A.M.E. Church and dwellings. The Pennsylvania Railroad crosses the upper middle of the sheet on a stone bridge over the river, in a broad band of tracks. At the right edge Murray Street ends at Sterling Place. The river banks on the west are marked 'See Volume Two'.
notes: Union Street west of Caldwell Place is now Elizabethtown Plaza.
Union County Court House, County Jail, First Presbyterian Church and its burying ground, and the Free Public Library (built 1911) are on this part.
The ground west of the Elizabeth River is in Volume Two.

turned sheet, two parts divided by a heavy diagonal line: part 1 civic centre (Broad, S. Broad, Rahway Av, Union St, Caldwell Pl, Murray St), part 2 strip north of the river (W. Jersey, Sterling Pl, Price St, Public Service Corp.); Elizabeth River, PRR stone bridge; See Volume Two.

sheet-13-2.description: The upper strip of sheet 13 is a separately placed part showing the ground between the Elizabeth River and Sterling Place, north of the river from the main part. It is bounded by Murray Street on the left, the river along the top of the sheet, and Price Street and the river on the right; West Jersey Street crosses it and Sterling Place runs along its lower edge. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the right of the page, and the same Murray Street and Sterling Place corner also appears at the right edge of the main part. Most of the strip is taken by the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey: the Public Service Railway Co. distribution headquarters and storage of line supplies on the river, with automatic sprinklers and a watchman, and the Public Service Electric Co. Elizabeth Sub-Station of fire-proof construction beside West Jersey Street. Trestles and sidings run in from the left. Along West Jersey Street and Price Street are frame dwellings, a Chinese laundry, a cobbler and a small store, and on Price Street a row of two-storey dwellings near the river. A heavy black line, the dividing line of the part, runs diagonally below Sterling Place and Price Street; Murray Street crosses the river on a bridge at the right. The river edge is lettered 'See Volume Two'.
notes: Public Service Corporation of N.J.: Public Service Railway Co. distribution headquarters and Public Service Electric Co. Elizabeth Sub-Station.

Placed by two hand-picked junctions (West Jersey Street / Sterling Place and Murray Street / Sterling Place); they imply 8.1 px/ft and a rotation 14 degrees off part 1, so modern Sterling Place is not on its 1922 line. Low confidence.
Price Street meets West Jersey Street about 36 m west of Sterling Place on the sheet; today the two junctions are 9 m apart.

turned sheet, two parts divided by a heavy diagonal line: part 1 civic centre (Broad, S. Broad, Rahway Av, Union St, Caldwell Pl, Murray St), part 2 strip north of the river (W. Jersey, Sterling Pl, Price St, Public Service Corp.); Elizabeth River, PRR stone bridge; See Volume Two.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers both banks of the Elizabeth River south of Broad Street, between Pearl Street on the west and Elizabeth Avenue on the east, from South Broad Street at the top to Bridge Street near the foot. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. The river winds down the middle of the sheet. West of it, along Pearl Street, are the St. James M.E. Church and chapel and frame dwellings on deep lots running down to the water; Williamson Street and Rector Street leave Pearl Street to the west, and Washington Avenue is shown at the top left. East of the river, on South Broad Street, stand the Fire Department house of Hook and Ladder Co. No. 1 and Engine Co. No. 1 and a Women's Club, with brick stores at the Broad Street corner. Elizabeth Avenue is lined with stores and dwellings, a Chinese laundry, a day nursery, a Salvation Army hall and the Eagles Home; behind them are the Henry Cook print shop, Sayer's Row, the Campbell Art Co. printing works, the large Standard Sanitary Pottery Co. works with its kilns, and the J. and S. S. Thompson coal and lumber yards on both sides of Bridge Street. Bridge Street crosses the river on a draw bridge. Jefferson Avenue and West and East Scott Places meet Elizabeth Avenue from the east. The ground west of Pearl Street is marked 'See Volume Two'.
notes: Bridge Street crosses the Elizabeth River on a draw bridge; it is drawn 35 ft wide east of the river and 50 ft west of it.
Standard Sanitary Pottery Co. works, Campbell Art Co., Henry Cook print shop and J. and S. S. Thompson coal and lumber yards.
Fire Department: Hook and Ladder Co. No. 1 and Engine Co. No. 1 on South Broad Street.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the blocks between East Jersey Street and Elizabeth Avenue in central Elizabeth, from West Scott Place on the west to Catherine Street on the east, crossed by East Scott Place and Morrel Street. Madison Avenue enters East Jersey Street from the north, Washington Street leaves West Scott Place to the west, and Bridge Street runs south from Elizabeth Avenue at the foot of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Between West and East Scott Places lies a long park (lettered Park), and south of Washington Street the City Hall with the city offices and police department occupies the narrow block between the two Scott Places. East of East Scott Place stand Christ Church with its rectory and parish hall, Public School No. 2 in the middle of the block, a dance hall, an auto repair shop, a second-hand furniture and upholstery shop, a printing shop and a drug store among two-storey frame dwellings. The block between Morrel and Catherine Streets is residential, with a confectionery building and a few stores along Elizabeth Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in every street, with widths lettered (100 ft for East Jersey Street, 87 to 95 ft for Elizabeth Avenue). The ground across East Jersey Street, Catherine Street and Elizabeth Avenue is left blank for sheets 10, 16, 14 and 31, and west of West Scott Place for sheet 8.
notes: West Scott Place and East Scott Place are now Winfield Scott Plaza and Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard.
Washington Street (between the Scott Places) is now Dickinson Street.
Morrel Street is now spelled Morrell Street.
City Hall with city offices and police department between the Scott Places; Christ Church with rectory and parish hall; Public School No. 2.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers two residential blocks in central Elizabeth between East Jersey Street on the north and Elizabeth Avenue on the south, bounded by Catherine Street on the west and Spring Street on the east and divided by Prospect Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The blocks are filled with closely spaced two- and three-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots facing Catherine, Prospect and Spring Streets, with private garages, coops and sheds in the yards. At the north end of the Catherine Street block stands the club house of the Young Men's Hebrew Association on East Jersey Street, and an automobile repair shop of concrete block lies behind the Catherine Street houses. Elizabeth Avenue is lined with brick stores and flats, several of hollow tile or brick-filled walls, and at the Spring Street corner a shirt waist factory with steam heat and electric power. On Spring Street are an automobile house and furniture storage building and a paint shop. A long narrow open shed crosses the eastern block diagonally. Water pipes are drawn in all the streets, with Elizabeth Avenue lettered 87 ft wide and Catherine Street 55 ft. The ground across East Jersey Street, Spring Street and Elizabeth Avenue is left blank for sheets 17, 25 and 31, and west of Catherine Street for sheet 15.
notes: Spring Street south of East Jersey Street is South Spring Street in OpenStreetMap at its Elizabeth Avenue end; its East Jersey Street junction was not detected (modern Spring Street turns into West Mravlag Place there).
Young Men's Hebrew Association club house on East Jersey Street.
Shirt waist factory at Elizabeth Avenue and Spring Street.
E. Jersey, Elizabeth Av, Catherine, Prospect, Spring St; one part.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers six residential blocks in central Elizabeth between East Grand Street at the top and East Jersey Street at the foot, from Catherine Street on the west to Reid Street on the east. Spring Street runs down the middle of the sheet, and William Street, Lafayette Street and Elizabeth Street cross it; Elizabeth Street ends at Spring Street. Oak Street and Prospect Street are lettered where they leave East Grand and East Jersey Streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The blocks between East Grand and Lafayette Streets are packed with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with stores, a bake house and a concrete-block garage on East Grand Street and the stuccoed Moravian Church on Lafayette Street near Reid Street. The block between Lafayette and Elizabeth Streets west of Spring Street holds the American Gas Furnace Co. works, with machine shops, storage, a tool room and a disused gas holder and gas machine house, besides a row of dwellings on Catherine Street. The two southern blocks, between Elizabeth Street and East Jersey Street, are thinly built: large detached dwellings on deep lots and much open ground, with a dwelling of cement walls. Water pipes are drawn in every street; Spring Street is lettered 50 to 60 ft wide and East Jersey Street 66 ft. Only the street edges of the neighbouring sheets 12, 19, 10, 18, 16 and 25 are shown around the margins.
notes: Elizabeth Street (between Lafayette and East Jersey Streets) is now Boudinot Place.
American Gas Furnace Co. machine shops and a disused gas holder between Lafayette and Elizabeth Streets.
Moravian Church on Lafayette Street near Reid Street.
Catherine Street and Reid Street run along the sheet edges; the Catherine Street junctions fall just off the image and were not used.
Spring Street / Boudinot Place excluded: the detector placed it about 12 ft off the drawn centre.
E. Grand, William, Lafayette, Elizabeth St, E. Jersey, Catherine, Spring, Reid St; American Gas Furnace Co.; one part.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers four blocks in central Elizabeth between East Grand Street at the top and East Jersey Street at the foot, from Reid Street on the west to Smith Street on the east, divided by Jaques Street and crossed by Lafayette Street. Livingston Street runs diagonally north-east from East Grand Street at the upper right, William Street enters Reid Street from the west, and Rebecca Place leaves Smith Street to the east. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The two northern blocks hold rows of two- and three-storey frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots, a few stores and a row of brick flats on Reid Street, with rows of concrete-block garages in the yards. The south-west block, between Reid and Jaques Streets below Lafayette Street, is taken by the Elizabeth General Hospital: the Nurses Home, the Blake Memorial, a frame hospital building with offices, a water tank, a coal vault and engine room, a hospital garage, and a large new fire-proof wing drawn 'from plans', with a note that all present frame buildings are to be replaced by fire-proof ones. The south-east block holds dwellings on Jaques and Smith Streets and, on East Jersey Street, St. Michael's School and a building with bowling alleys, assembly room and club rooms. Water pipes are drawn in every street, with widths of 60 ft lettered for most of them and 70 ft for East Jersey Street.
notes: Jaques Street is spelled Jacques Street today.
Elizabeth General Hospital with the Nurses Home and Blake Memorial; a new fire-proof wing is drawn from plans.
St. Michael's School and a club building with bowling alleys on East Jersey Street.
E. Grand, Livingston, William, Lafayette, Rebecca Pl, E. Jersey, Reid, Jaques, Smith St; Elizabeth General Hospital; one part.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers part of central Elizabeth between Spring Street at the left and Henry Street at the right, from Anna Street at the top to East Grand Street at the bottom. The upper half is two long residential blocks between Anna, Bond and Magnolia Avenue, lined with two-storey frame dwellings, many of them stuccoed, with a few stores and automobile houses. Their western ends are institutional: the Sacred Heart School stands on the north side of Bond Street, and the Sacred Heart Roman Catholic Church with its tower and rectory faces Spring Street across Bond, next to the large T-shaped St. Walburgh Convent and its laundry. Below Magnolia Avenue the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet in a broad band of tracks, carried over Spring Street and Reid Street on iron bridges, with a signal tower beside the Reid Street bridge. North of the tracks the United States Leather Co. leather warehouse (fire-proof construction, built 1919, reinforced concrete) and the adjoining Central Leather Co. sole leather storage, cutting and shipping building line a covered platform along the railroad. South of the tracks Broadway runs at a slant from Spring Street towards Reid Street, with dwellings, stores, a wagon shed and the Mount Zion Chapel (Christian Science) in the block down to East Grand Street. East of Reid Street the Hyman Issacs Sons (as printed) old iron yard fills the ground between the tracks and East Grand Street, beside John Howson and Son, stair builders, with a woodworking shop and lumber shed. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along every street; a compass rose sits in the rail yard, and Jaques and Livingston Streets are lettered just below the lower right corner.
notes: Broadway between Spring and Reid Streets survives as the street now named Praise the Lord Plaza in OpenStreetMap.
Spring Street is now a divided trunk road (two one-way carriageways); its modern junctions lie 3 to 4.5 m east of the drawn street, so it was left out of the control.
Jaques Street is spelled Jacques Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses Spring and Reid Streets on iron bridges.
United States Leather Co. warehouse, built 1919 of reinforced concrete, and Central Leather Co. cutting and storage building stand on the north side of the tracks.
Sacred Heart R.C. Church, Sacred Heart School and St. Walburgh Convent occupy the western ends of the blocks on Bond Street.
Hyman Issacs Sons old iron yard and John Howson and Son, stair builders, lie between the tracks and East Grand Street.
Anna, Bond, Magnolia, Spring, Henry, Reid, Broadway, East Grand; CRR of NJ; Sacred Heart church, school and convent; US Leather / Central Leather. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, continues sheet 19 eastward through central Elizabeth, from Henry Street at the left edge to Division Street at the right edge and from Anna Street at the top to East Grand Street at the bottom. The two blocks between Anna, Bond and Magnolia Avenue are long residential blocks with scattered two-storey frame dwellings, some stuccoed, many vacant lots and a few automobile houses, coops and sheds; one lot holds only a foundation. The eastern half of the block between Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue is industrial: the Foster, Heaton Co. dye manufactory (products for making azo dyes, with offices and laboratory and a dry house) and the large Bronze Powder Works Co. plant, with stamping, polishing, grinding and tumbler rooms, cleaning and raw material storage, paint shops, a carpenter shop, a foundry with concrete walls, a coal bin and coal shed, and an office, all numbered as separate buildings. South of Magnolia Avenue the sole leather storage, cutting and shipping building of the United States Leather Co. and Central Leather Co. extends in from sheet 19 at the left, and the Jenkins Bros. rubber division works, with its manufacturing building, dry room, mixing and drying rooms, laboratory, engine room and a railroad track on trestle, stands against Division Street at the right. The main line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet as a wide band of tracks, with a branch curving away to the south-west, and passes under Division Street on an iron bridge. Below the tracks the ground to East Grand Street is mostly vacant; Hyman Isaacs Sons iron and metals yard and J. R. O'Connor's vegetable storage lie at the lower left near Livingston Street, and Broadway is lettered at the bottom edge.
notes: Henry Street runs along the left edge and Division Street along the right edge; both are cut by the sheet edge near their centrelines.
Division Street is lettered 80 ft wide; the other streets 60 ft.
The Bronze Powder Works Co. and the Foster, Heaton Co. dye works occupy the eastern half of the block between Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue.
Jenkins Bros. rubber division (Mutual risk) stands on Magnolia Avenue at Division Street, beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey.

Anna, Bond, Magnolia, Henry (left edge), Division (right edge), East Grand; Bronze Powder Works, Foster Heaton dye works, Jenkins Bros. rubber; CRR of NJ. One part.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the left, covers part of south-central Elizabeth between Third Avenue at the top and the Elizabeth River at the bottom, with Spring Street running diagonally across the upper left and High Street along the right. The upper half holds three residential blocks between Third and Fourth Avenues: the wedge between Spring and South Streets, lined along Spring Street with small two-storey frame dwellings with brick-filled partitions; the block between South and Center Streets, with frame flats and dwellings, a bakery and a cement block works; and the block between Center and High Streets, of small frame dwellings, stores and automobile houses. Below Fourth Avenue, South Street bends to the south-west and crosses the Elizabeth River on a drawbridge to a junction with Pearl Street. Between South Street, Fourth Avenue and the river lies the storage and supply depot of the Elizabethtown Gas Light Co., with the Rotary Meter Co. as tenants in its assembling and testing buildings, a pipe shed and other sheds. The block between Center and High Streets south of Fourth Avenue has a few dwellings, a club room and the storage of contractors' equipment on Fourth Avenue, and is otherwise laid out in empty lots running down to the river; Fifth Avenue, marked not opened, ends at the river beyond High Street. The Elizabeth River crosses the lower part of the sheet from left to right. The strip south of the river, with Pearl Street and Norwood Terrace, is left blank and lettered 'See Volume Two'. Reid Street enters the top margin at the upper left, and a compass rose stands in the open ground at the left.
notes: Center Street is Centre Street in OpenStreetMap; Spring Street here is South Spring Street.
Fifth Avenue is marked 'not opened' beyond High Street.
South Street crosses the Elizabeth River on a drawbridge.
Elizabethtown Gas Light Co. storage and supply depot, with the Rotary Meter Co. as tenants, lies between South Street and the river.
The area south of the river is left blank and lettered 'See Volume Two'.
The sheet is drawn with north towards the left of the page (rotation about -66 degrees).
Fourth Avenue, South Street and Spring Street meet at one junction; the modern node for South Spring Street was left out to avoid counting it twice.
3rd, 4th, 5th (not opened) Ave; Spring, South, Center, High; Elizabeth River with the South St drawbridge; south of the river blank ("See Volume Two"). Turned, north to the left. One part.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the left of the page, continues sheet 21 eastward in south-central Elizabeth, from High Street at the left edge to Amity Street at the right edge and from Third Avenue at the top to the Elizabeth River at the bottom. Between Third and Fourth Avenues four blocks are divided by South Seventh Street, Christine Street and John Street, which runs at a slant and is lettered 85 ft wide at Third Avenue and 50 ft further down. These blocks are densely built with two-storey frame dwellings, flats and stores, several of them stuccoed or brick, with a moving picture theatre on High Street at Third Avenue, a tailor shop, a plumbers' supplies store and plumbers' shop, a bake house, a hall, and a junk yard with rag storage near Amity Street. South of Fourth Avenue building thins out: a bakery and wagon house near High Street, a cement block works, rags storage, an auto and wagon shed, another bakery, brick storage buildings along John Street and a green house, with dwellings along Fourth Avenue and Amity Street; the rest is open lots running down to the river. Fifth Avenue, marked not opened, ends at a boat house on the river bank, where a shed holds storage of second-hand building material. The Elizabeth River crosses the bottom of the sheet, and the ground south of it is left blank and lettered 'See Volume Two'. A compass rose is drawn at the top in the margin between the blocks of sheet 24.
notes: Fifth Avenue is marked 'not opened'.
John Street is lettered 85 ft wide at Third Avenue and 50 ft wide south of it.
Line work on this sheet is faint in places; most junctions were hand-picked from the drawn block edges.
The area south of the river is left blank and lettered 'See Volume Two'.
The sheet is drawn with north towards the left of the page (rotation about -66 degrees).
3rd to 5th Ave, High, S. 7th, Christine, John, Amity; Elizabeth River; south of the river blank. Faint lines. One part.

sheet-23-1.description: The main part of sheet 23, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the left of the page, covers part of south-central Elizabeth between Elizabeth Avenue and Third Avenue, from South Reid Street at the left to High Street at the right. Elizabeth Avenue crosses the upper half diagonally; the ground beyond it, belonging to sheets 25 and 26, is left blank apart from the ends of Smith Street and Jaques Street. In the wedge between Elizabeth Avenue, South Street and Second Avenue stand a row of brick stores with a Chinese laundry, a hardware store and a drug store, an auto sales room and a service station with an underground gasoline tank. Between Elizabeth Avenue, Center Street, High Street and Second Avenue lies a block of dwellings and stores with a Police Department automobile house facing Center Street and stores on Elizabeth Avenue at First Avenue. Below Second Avenue three blocks run down to Third Avenue: the triangular block between South Reid Street and South Street, with small frame dwellings along South Reid Street and an undertaker on South Street; the block between South and Center Streets, with dwellings, an auto repair shop and St. Anthony's Roman Catholic Church and its house; and the block between Center and High Streets, with dwellings, an auto repair garage of cement block and the Reliable Wood Working Co. building used for trouser manufacturing. Almost all buildings are two-storey frame dwellings, some stuccoed. The upper left corner of the sheet is given to a separate inset (part 2) behind a heavy line, and a compass rose sits on that line.
notes: Center Street is Centre Street and Jaques Street is Jacques Street in OpenStreetMap.
Elizabeth Avenue is lettered 86 ft and 77 ft wide; the north side of the avenue (sheets 25 and 26) is left blank.
St. Anthony's R.C. Church stands between South and Center Streets near Third Avenue.
A Police Department automobile house stands on Center Street near Elizabeth Avenue.
Reliable Wood Working Co. building, used for trouser manufacturing, on High Street.

1st to 3rd Ave, Elizabeth Ave, Smith, Jaques, S. Reid, South, Center, High; St. Anthony's R.C. church. Two parts: part 2 is an inset at the upper left behind a heavy line (block between Elizabeth Ave, Spring, S. Reid and 3rd Ave).

sheet-23-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 23 is an inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, set off by a heavy line, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the left like the main map. It shows one block that lies on the ground away from the rest of the sheet, north-west of the main map and just north of the upper left corner of sheet 21: the triangular block bounded by Elizabeth Avenue at the top, Spring Street at the lower left, South Reid Street at the right and Third Avenue at the bottom. Along Elizabeth Avenue stands a row of two-storey brick stores, some of hollow tile, numbered 940 to 954, with a stuccoed store at the corner of Spring Street and a concrete-block dwelling (950 C) behind them. In the middle of the block, facing Spring Street, are a blacksmith and auto repair shop of cement block with a cement floor and an adjoining welding and brazing shop, a machine shop and a storage and shipping building. South Reid Street is lined with two- and three-storey frame dwellings numbered 7 to 29, and two dwellings (927 and 929) face Third Avenue. The rest of the block is open lots. Sheet numbers 23, 21, 25 and 31 printed around the block show which sheets adjoin it. Elizabeth Avenue is lettered 85 ft wide, South Reid Street and Third Avenue 60 ft.
notes: The inset is drawn out of position: the block lies north-west of the main map, next to the upper left corner of sheet 21.
Spring Street is South Spring Street in OpenStreetMap; it is now a divided trunk road, and its junctions fit about 4 m off the drawn street.
Only one junction (Third Avenue / Spring Street) lies inside the inset; the other control points are drawn centrelines extended a short way past its edges, so the placement is low confidence.
Blacksmith and auto repair shop with welding, brazing and machine shops in the middle of the block.

1st to 3rd Ave, Elizabeth Ave, Smith, Jaques, S. Reid, South, Center, High; St. Anthony's R.C. church. Two parts: part 2 is an inset at the upper left behind a heavy line (block between Elizabeth Ave, Spring, S. Reid and 3rd Ave).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the left of the page, covers part of south-central Elizabeth from Elizabeth Avenue and First Avenue at the top to Third Avenue at the bottom, and from High Street at the left edge to Amity Street at the right edge, with South Seventh Street, Christine Street and John Street between. The scan is lighter and more yellow than its neighbours. In the upper left corner a short strip of Elizabeth Avenue between High and Seventh Streets is drawn in its own outline: a brick building with a bank on the first floor, offices on the second and a lodge room on the third, a plumber, stores of concrete block, a lunch room and a club house. The blocks between First and Second Avenues hold mostly two-storey frame dwellings, some stuccoed or of hollow tile, with the Arny Steel Construction Co. fabricating shop, the Triangle Mfg. Co. trouser factory, a furniture warehouse and a blacksmith on the High Street block; a concrete-block garage for 30 cars, a cement block works and a Baby Welfare Station on the Seventh Street block; two halls on the Christine Street block; and an auto and monument works shop on the John Street block. Between Second and Third Avenues stand Public School No. 3 with its auditorium, the open City Play Ground No. 3 with a field house, which fills the whole block between Seventh and Christine Streets, and the Italian Methodist Episcopal Church with its gymnasium at John Street and Amity Street, among dwellings, stores, a pool room, a bakery, a lumber shed and an old shed. A compass rose stands in the playground.
notes: Public School No. 3 stands on High Street at Second Avenue.

Italian M.E. Church with a gymnasium at Second Avenue and Amity Street.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the right of the page, covers three blocks of central Elizabeth on the east side of Elizabeth Avenue, from Spring Street at the top to Smith Street at the bottom and from Elizabeth Avenue at the left to East Jersey Street at the right, with Reid Street and Jaques Street between them. Elizabeth Avenue, lettered 85 to 87 ft wide, is lined with three-storey brick stores numbered 853 to 959, among them a hardware store, a furniture store, a drug store, a bake house with flour storage, the I.O.O.F. Hall on the third floor of 909, and a public garage for 40 cars with buried gasoline tanks near Spring Street. Behind this frontage the blocks are residential, with two-storey frame dwellings, many plastered or stuccoed, along Spring, Reid, Jaques and Smith Streets, and East Jersey Street. Institutions fill the middle of the block between Reid and Jaques Streets: Public School No. 9 on Jaques Street, class rooms, the German Lutheran Parish House with bowling alleys, and a synagogue on East Jersey Street. St. Michael's Roman Catholic Church with its slated spire stands at Smith Street and East Jersey Street. Smaller works include a plumber's shop, an automobile house and storage building, an oil house and a concrete-block bakery. At the lower left, Second Avenue and South Street meet Elizabeth Avenue at a small triangle; the blocks across Elizabeth Avenue (sheet 23) and the far sides of Spring, East Jersey and Smith Streets (sheets 16, 17, 18 and 26) are left blank, with Cross Street and Martin Street lettered at the bottom edge. A compass rose stands at the upper left.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right of the page, covers part of central Elizabeth south of Smith Street, from Elizabeth Avenue at the left to East Jersey Street at the right and down to Seventh Street at the bottom. Cross Street and Martin Street run down the sheet, Port Street crosses the middle, and New Point Road cuts diagonally from Elizabeth Avenue to the lower right, with Marshall Street, Division Street, Miller Street, Franklin Street and Fulton Street at its lower end. Elizabeth Avenue, lettered 80 to 86 ft wide, is lined with two- and three-storey brick stores numbered 801 to 847, among them a moving picture theatre of stuccoed concrete block, two bake houses with ovens, a hardware and paints store, a bank, a restaurant and a smoke house; at its junction with New Point Road a fire-proof bank of reinforced concrete built in 1921 stands at the head of a block that also holds the Delpark Inc. Factory No. 3 collar factory. The blocks between Cross Street, Martin Street and East Jersey Street are residential, with two-storey frame dwellings, the Swedish Lutheran Church on Martin Street near Smith Street, and the Elizabeth Paper Box Co. factory with a shirt waist factory on Cross Street at Port Street. Between Port Street and New Point Road stand Fire Department Hook and Ladder Co. No. 3 and Engine No. 3 with a hose tower, and the large Turnhalle Vorwaerts with bowling alleys, a stage and a gymnasium. Further down New Point Road are an auto repair shop of concrete block with a machine shop, a dyeing and cleaning shop and scattered dwellings and stores along Division and Miller Streets. Centre Street and First Avenue are lettered across Elizabeth Avenue at the left, and the ground beyond Seventh Street (sheet 57) is left blank.
notes: Port Street is Bank Street in OpenStreetMap.
Fire Department Hook and Ladder Co. No. 3 and Engine No. 3 stand between Port Street and New Point Road.
