sheet-27.description: Sheet 27, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the lower left of the page, covers part of central Elizabeth between Smith Street at the left and Division Street at the right, from East Grand Street and Broadway at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom. The upper part is given over to the railroad and street railway: the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along Broadway, lettered 100 ft wide, and the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey (Public Service Electric Co.) Elizabeth car house occupies the block at the upper left with its office and a large car barn used for car repairing and storage, beside an auto repair and body shop, a cobbler and a barber. Open car yards lie between Livingston Street and Broadway, crossed by Port Street, marked not opened. Near Division Street are the Elizabeth Roofing Co. with a storage shed and a carpenter shop. Below Livingston Street the sheet is residential: two-storey frame dwellings line Livingston and Lafayette Streets, Rebecca Place and East Jersey Street, with a cleaning and pressing shop, work shops, an ice house, a green house and a motorcycle shed. The Gnome Machine and Tool Co. and the Columbia Pattern Works, with a brass foundry, stand at the junction of Livingston Street and Rebecca Place near Division Street. St. Andrew's Chapel, with a belfry, and its Sunday school face Division Street between Rebecca Place and East Jersey Street, and brick stores stand at the corner of East Jersey and Division. Trumbull Street is lettered at the upper right, and a compass rose sits in the open ground at the left.
notes: Port Street, between Livingston Street and Broadway, is marked 'not opened'.
Broadway along the Central Railroad of New Jersey is lettered 100 ft wide; Broadway east of Reid Street no longer exists as a street in OpenStreetMap.
Public Service Electric Co. Elizabeth car house with a car barn, open day and night.
Gnome Machine and Tool Co. and Columbia Pattern Works on Livingston Street near Division Street.
St. Andrew's Chapel and Sunday school on Division Street.
Elizabeth Roofing Co. near Division Street and Broadway.
Division / East Grand / Trumbull and Division / Rebecca Place fit with residuals of about 2.6 m along Division Street.
Smith, East Grand, Broadway, Livingston, Port (not opened), Lafayette, Rebecca Pl, E. Jersey, Division, Trumbull; Public Service car house and car yards, St. Andrew's Chapel. One part.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers an irregular wedge of south-central Elizabeth between Trumbull Street and Court Street at the top and East Jersey Street at the bottom, with Division Street on the west and 7th Street on the east. The blocks are cut diagonally by South Park Street, by Broadway, which runs beside the 100-ft right of way of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, and by Livingston Street; Miller Street crosses the lower half and Rebecca Place leaves Division Street to the west. The area is a mix of small industry, yards and frame housing. Industrial premises include the American Metal Treatment Co. metal treating and machine works (with case hardening and tempering furnaces) on South Park Street, the Dalvin Chemical Co. manufacturers of food colors (noted as plant closed and in hands of receiver), Tokers coal yard with a reinforced concrete coal pocket and a trestle off the railroad, the Elizabeth Auto Parts Mfg. Co. machine shop, lumber piles at 7th Street and Livingston Street, a contractors' storage yard and a pattern shop and cutlery works on Miller Street. Most other buildings are two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings and automobile sheds, in rows along South Park Street, Livingston Street and East Jersey Street; a pair of brick stores stands at East Jersey Street and 7th Street. Railroad sidings fan out from the main line across Broadway. Large parts of blocks 1 and 2 are empty lots. Water pipes of 6 to 20 inches are drawn in most streets, and the sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with the north arrow pointing up and to the left.
notes: Broadway, drawn alongside the Central Railroad of New Jersey between South Park Street and Livingston Street, is not in the modern street network here.
Miller Street jogs at Livingston Street: it is 30 ft wide north of Livingston and 25 ft south of it, and the two halves do not line up.
Trumbull Street is lettered 80 ft wide; only its south side is drawn in full.
The Dalvin Chemical Co. plant is noted as closed and in the hands of a receiver.
map, 50 ft. Trumbull, Court, South Park, Broadway (along CRR of NJ, gone), Livingston, E. Jersey, Division, Miller, 7th, Rebecca Pl. One part.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 is drawn at 60 ft to an inch and covers the long blocks between Division Street on the west and 7th Street on the east, from Anna Street at the top down to Trumbull Street, with a strip south of Trumbull Street that repeats the top of sheet 28 (South Park Street, Court Street and 7th Street). Anna Street, Bond Street, York Street and Port Avenue, which cuts diagonally across the north-east corner of the first block, are all marked as not opened, and the two upper blocks are drawn completely empty. The block between York Street and Trumbull Street is filled by the yard of the Central Railroad of New Jersey: some twenty tracks enter from the west on an iron bridge over Division Street and fan out eastward across the whole width of the sheet toward sheet 30. The only buildings in the yard are a small office, a water tank by Division Street and a row of tool houses with a second office beside the southern tracks. South of Trumbull Street a club house and two frame dwellings stand at the corner of Court Street. The neighbouring sheets 89 and 90 are indicated at the top, sheet 20 to the west and sheet 30 to the east. The street widths are lettered as 80 ft for Division, York and Trumbull Streets, 60 ft for Anna, Bond, Court and 7th Streets and 70 ft for Port Avenue.
notes: Drawn at 60 ft to an inch, not the 50 ft of the city sheets.
Anna Street, Bond Street, York Street and Port Avenue are marked not opened; the two blocks between them are empty.
York Street lines up with today's Magnolia Avenue where it meets Division Street.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses Division Street on an iron bridge and fans out into a yard of about twenty tracks; the yard is gone today.
Placed from two detected junctions on 7th Street and five hand-picked ones on Division Street and Trumbull Street, where only the east side of Division Street is drawn.

map, 60 ft to an inch. CRR of NJ yard between York and Trumbull, Division to 7th; Anna, Bond, York, Port Av not opened (blocks empty). One part; Division drawn one side only; mostly hand-picked control.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 is drawn at 60 ft to an inch and continues sheet 29 eastward, covering the blocks between 7th Street on the west and 6th Street on the east from Anna Street at the top to Trumbull Street. Anna Street, Bond Street, York Street and Port Avenue, which crosses the second row of blocks diagonally, are all marked as not opened, and blocks 1, 2 and 3 are drawn empty. The whole block between York Street and Trumbull Street, block 4, is the yard of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn as about seventy parallel tracks running the full width of the sheet, with a few crossovers at the east edge where the yard continues on sheet 75; 7th Street and 6th Street are shown only as short stubs entering the yard from either side. There are no buildings on the sheet. Along the bottom, south of Trumbull Street, the sheet repeats the street pattern of sheet 63: Seventh Street and Magnolia Avenue leaving Trumbull Street at the south-west corner, Bond Street running diagonally away from Trumbull Street in the middle and Sixth Street at the east, with water pipes of 10 and 12 inches in Trumbull Street and Seventh Street. The neighbouring sheets 90 (north), 29 (west), 75 (east) and 63 (south) are indicated around the edges. Widths are lettered as 60 ft for Anna, Bond, 7th and 6th Streets and 80 ft for York and Trumbull Streets.
notes: Drawn at 60 ft to an inch.
Anna Street, Bond Street, York Street and Port Avenue are marked not opened; the blocks between them are empty.
The block between York Street and Trumbull Street is entirely the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard; it is gone today.
Bond Street south of Trumbull Street does not meet Trumbull Street where today's Bond Street does: the hand-picked junction was about 9 m off the modern node and was left out.
Placed from only two junctions, both on Trumbull Street (7th Street and 6th Street), as a helmert transformation; the upper part of the sheet rests on that line alone.
map, 60 ft to an inch. CRR of NJ yard continued, 7th to 6th St; Anna, Bond, York, Port Av not opened; no buildings. One part; helmert on Trumbull row only (low confidence).

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the land on both sides of a large bend of the Elizabeth River south of Elizabeth Avenue, between Pearl Street on the west and Spring Street on the east, with South Street along the bottom where the river is crossed by a draw bridge. The north side of the sheet is a dense row of buildings on the south side of Elizabeth Avenue (numbers 1000 to 1082, the avenue lettered 87 ft wide), opposite the ends of Catherine Street and Prospect Street. Along the avenue and behind it are the J. and S.S. Thompson lumber and coal yard with lumber sheds and piles, T.F. and H.C. Sayre masons' materials and cement block works, two large garages (one for 40 cars), a cement block factory, a plumbers' supply store, the Clauss Bottling Co. with syrup mixing, bottling and washing buildings, an undertaker, a printing and carpenter shop and a blacksmith. The largest building is the Meccano Co. Inc. assembly plant for mechanical toys, of mill construction, running back from the avenue beside the City Yard. Along Spring Street are brick stores and dwellings, the Nat Levy and Co. underwear factory, Green furniture storage and the Bullet Proof and Non-Shatterable Glass Corp.; near South Street stand a rabbit fur dressing shop and buildings damaged by fire. The inside of the river bend (block 3) is largely open land, with a row of frame dwellings along the curving east side of Pearl Street and Cameron Place leading west; the area west of Pearl Street is marked to see volume two. Third Avenue and South Street leave Spring Street at the east edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Spring Street south of Elizabeth Avenue is today's South Spring Street; Pearl Street is today's South Pearl Street; Third Avenue is today's 3rd Avenue.
Catherine Street is lettered "Cathrine St." on the sheet.
Prospect Street meets Elizabeth Avenue about 14 m from where today's Prospect Street does; it was left out of the control.
Cameron Place is not in the modern street network.
South Street crosses the Elizabeth River on a draw bridge.
The Meccano Co. Inc. mechanical toy assembly plant and the Bullet Proof and Non-Shatterable Glass Corp. stand on this sheet.
The area west of Pearl Street is left blank with the note "See Volume Two".

map, 50 ft. Elizabeth Av, Catherine, Prospect, Spring, Third Av, South St, Pearl, Cameron Pl; Elizabeth River bend with draw bridge; Meccano Co., Clauss Bottling, Nat Levy underwear. One part; "See Volume Two" west of Pearl.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and covers the thinly built south-western edge of the city between the Elizabeth River on the west and 4th Avenue on the east, from Amity Street at the top to Atlantic Street and Baltic Street at the bottom. A grid of east-west streets crosses it: Palmer, Niles, Spencer, South 5th, Loomis, Redcliffe (formerly Hart) and Doyle (formerly Coote) Streets, then Atlantic Street, with 5th Avenue running north-south through the middle; 5th Avenue is marked not opened at its north end. Most of the blocks are drawn only as rows of narrow empty building lots, and the large blocks between the river and 5th Avenue are almost entirely open. Buildings are few: frame dwellings and sheds along 4th Avenue and Amity Street, the Charles Farm with its barns, wagon shed and milk house on Niles Street, and the Micheal Tussel Farm with a concrete block milk house, wagon shed, coop and a stuccoed dwelling on 4th Avenue near Redcliffe Street. The Elizabeth River winds down the west side of the sheet in a broad loop; South 5th Street crosses it on an iron bridge to Summer Avenue, with Arnet Street, Garden Street and Brunswick Avenue shown on the far bank. The neighbouring sheets 22, 33, 34, 47, 42, 40 and 38 are indicated around the edges, and Hoffman Street is noted as the old name for the continuation of Redcliffe Street beyond 4th Avenue.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch.
Redcliffe Street is lettered with its former name Hart in brackets, Doyle Street with Coote, and Hoffman Street is given in brackets east of 4th Avenue.
5th Avenue is marked not opened north of Spencer Street.
Atlantic Street is drawn straight; today's Atlantic Street follows a different, curved line here and was left out of the control.
South 5th Street crosses the Elizabeth River on an iron bridge to Summer Avenue.
The west half of the sheet has no control points; it is placed by the fit to the junctions on 4th and 5th Avenues.

map, 100 ft. Elizabeth River, Amity, Palmer, Niles, Spencer, S. 5th, Loomis, Redcliffe (Hart), Doyle (Coote), Atlantic, Baltic, 4th and 5th Avs; mostly empty lots, Charles Farm, Micheal Tussel Farm. One part.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 is a residential sheet in the south-central part of the city, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. It covers the blocks between 2nd Avenue (top), 3rd Avenue (middle) and 4th Avenue (bottom), crossed by Amity Street at the west edge, Palmer Street, Niles Street, Spencer Street and South 5th Street at the east edge. The blocks are lined with two-storey frame dwellings, many of them stuccoed, a few on hollow tile, with rows of small brick stores at the 3rd Avenue and 4th Avenue corners and frame tenements on 4th Avenue and South 5th Street. Back lots hold automobile sheds, stables, coops and storage sheds. Small businesses include two bakeries with ovens (on Amity Street at 2nd Avenue and on Amity Street near 4th Avenue), a concrete block garage for 25 cars on 3rd Avenue, a concert room, an umbrella factory with electric motor power and a plumber's shop on Palmer Street, junk yards on Palmer Street and on Spencer Street (the latter with scrap shears and a rag store) and a mason's storage yard on Niles Street. The largest building is the Christopher Columbus Public School, of brick with hollow tile partition walls, heated by steam and lit by electricity, at the corner of 3rd Avenue and South 5th Street; the rest of that block (block 4) is drawn as empty lots. Water pipes of 4 to 20 inches are shown in every street. The neighbouring sheets 35 (north), 24 and 22 (west), 34 (east) and 32 (south) are indicated around the edges.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper left and the avenues run across the page.
Christopher Columbus Public School stands at 3rd Avenue and South 5th Street.
Junctions on 4th Avenue were mostly not detected; the bottom row is controlled by 4th Avenue at Spencer Street and at South 5th Street only.
map, 50 ft, turned (north upper left). 2nd, 3rd, 4th Avs x Amity, Palmer, Niles, Spencer, S. 5th; Christopher Columbus Public School. One part.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 continues sheet 33 eastward in the south-central part of the city, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. It covers the blocks between 2nd Avenue (top), 3rd Avenue (middle) and 4th Avenue (bottom), from South 5th Street at the west edge to Atlantic Street at the east edge, crossed by Loomis Street, by Rankin Street north of 3rd Avenue and by Redcliffe Street (formerly Hoffman) and Doyle Street south of it; Rankin Street and Redcliffe Street do not line up at 3rd Avenue. The part north of 3rd Avenue is built up with two-storey frame dwellings, a few stores and brick or concrete block houses, with automobile sheds and stables behind. A large junk business occupies the block between South 5th Street and Loomis Street, with junk yards, junk storage, an office and scales, wagon sheds and a long shed, and a milk house stands nearby. South of 3rd Avenue the corner of South 5th Street holds a frame synagogue lit by electricity and heated by a stove, a further junk yard and a concrete block manufacturing shed; the rest of the southern blocks (4 to 7) are drawn mostly as rows of empty building lots, with only a few dwellings on Loomis Street and a pair of concrete block buildings at 3rd Avenue and Atlantic Street. Block 2, between Loomis Street and Rankin Street north of 3rd Avenue, is also largely empty lots. Water pipes of 6 to 20 inches are drawn in the streets. The neighbouring sheets 36 (north), 33 (west), 47 (east) and 32 (south) are indicated, and the old names Hart Street and Coote Street are noted at the bottom edge.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper left.
Redcliffe Street is lettered with the old name Hoffman in brackets; Hart Street and Coote Street are given in brackets at the bottom edge for the continuations of Redcliffe Street and Doyle Street.
Rankin Street (north of 3rd Avenue) and Redcliffe Street and Doyle Street (south of it) are offset from each other at 3rd Avenue.
A synagogue stands at South 5th Street and 3rd Avenue.
2nd Avenue / Loomis Street was hand-picked; the detector placed it about 14 ft east of the drawn centre.
map, 50 ft, turned. 2nd, 3rd, 4th Avs x S. 5th, Loomis, Rankin, Redcliffe (Hoffman), Doyle, Atlantic; synagogue, junk yards. One part.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 is a residential sheet in the south-central part of the city, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. It covers one row of blocks between Elizabeth Avenue and 1st Avenue, from 6th Street on the west to 5th Street on the east, and a second row between 1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue, crossed by Amity Street (at the west edge), Palmer Street, Niles Street, Spencer Street and South 5th Street. The large block between Elizabeth Avenue and 1st Avenue holds the parish of the Holy Rosary: the Roman Catholic Church of the Holy Rosary, the School of the Holy Rosary and a brick Sisters' Home, all heated by steam and lit by gas. Elsewhere on this block are stores and dwellings along Elizabeth Avenue, a brick undertaker's building, a club, a cobbler, a plumber's shop and a vacant store at 5th Street. West of 6th Street, in a strip repeating sheet 51, are the German Methodist Episcopal Church with its parsonage, a furniture store and a storage building of hollow tile. The blocks between 1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue are lined almost entirely with two-storey frame dwellings, with a few brick stores at the corners, a concrete block garage for 10 cars at 1st Avenue and Niles Street, a row of brick dwellings on Spencer Street and a mission room on South 5th Street. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn in all the streets. The neighbouring sheets 52 (north), 51 and 24 (west), 36 (east) and 33 (south) are indicated.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper left.
The Roman Catholic Church of the Holy Rosary, the School of the Holy Rosary and the Sisters' Home occupy the block between Elizabeth Avenue and 1st Avenue.
The German Methodist Episcopal Church and parsonage stand west of 6th Street.
1st Avenue / Amity Street was detected but disagreed with the fit by about 11 m and was left out.
map, 50 ft, turned. Elizabeth, 1st, 2nd Avs x 6th, Amity, Palmer, Niles, Spencer, 5th/S. 5th; R.C. Church and School of the Holy Rosary, German M.E. Church. One part.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 continues sheet 35 eastward, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Its top row is the long block between Elizabeth Avenue and 1st Avenue from 5th Street to 4th Street; below 1st Avenue the blocks run to 2nd Avenue between South 5th Street, Loomis Street, Rankin Street, Atlantic Street and Baltic Street at the east edge. Elizabeth Avenue is lettered 80 ft wide and 1st Avenue 75 ft. The Elizabeth Avenue frontage is a row of stores and dwellings, with bowling alleys at the corner of 5th Street, a bake shop, a blacksmith and storage buildings behind, and two-storey frame dwellings along 1st Avenue. The block between Loomis Street and Rankin Street is dominated by the Elizabeth Junior High School, a steel-framed brick building with an auditorium, wood working and printing shops and a boiler and engine room, drawn from plans; beside it on 1st Avenue is the Henry Rosenbaum and Co. shirt factory with its shipping room. At 2nd Avenue and Baltic Street stands the Atlantic Romper Co. Inc. factory. The rest of the blocks are lined with two-storey frame dwellings, a few stuccoed or brick, with sheds and automobile sheds behind; the south end of the block between South 5th Street and Loomis Street is drawn as empty lots. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn in the streets. The neighbouring sheets 53 (north), 35 (west), 49 (east), 34 and 47 (south) are indicated.
notes: The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper left.
Elizabeth Junior High School, drawn from plans, occupies most of the block between Loomis Street and Rankin Street.
4th Street jogs where it crosses Elizabeth Avenue; the junction was hand-picked midway between its two halves.
1st Avenue / Atlantic Street and 1st Avenue / 4th Street were hand-picked; the detector paired the wrong lines at Atlantic Street.
Baltic Street, at the east edge, is not in the modern street network here.
map, 50 ft, turned. Elizabeth, 1st, 2nd Avs x 5th/S. 5th, Loomis, Rankin, Atlantic, 4th, Baltic; Elizabeth Junior High School, Rosenbaum shirt factory, Atlantic Romper Co. One part.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the Bayway district at the south-western edge of the city, where it meets Linden Township. Allen Avenue runs down the left edge along the city line, with Klem Avenue lettered on the township side; Edgar Road crosses the top of the sheet, with the area beyond it marked "See Volume Two". Bay Way runs down the middle of the sheet, 80 ft wide, and Summer Avenue runs diagonally from Bay Way to the lower right; the open ground east of Summer Avenue is also left blank for Volume Two. Grier Avenue crosses the sheet below the middle. To the south lie Myrtle Street, Morses Mill Road (running diagonally between Myrtle and Bay Way), Bedle Place, E Street and South Broad Street, which runs along the bottom at the left and then diagonally up to Summer Avenue at the right, with Maple Avenue, D Street and Britton Street beyond it. Washington Avenue, at the top, and Myrtle Street north of Grier Avenue are marked "not opened". Most of the sheet is laid out in narrow numbered lots, many still empty; the built lots hold small frame dwellings, coops and sheds. The densest building is along South Broad Street near Summer Avenue, with stores, a plumbing shop, a Pentecostal church and a cement block works. A cottage named "Bayway Cottage" stands on Bay Way at E Street. Water pipes are drawn along most streets. The compass rose sits in the blank Volume Two area at the upper right and the scale bar at the lower left.
notes: E Street is now Bonnett Street and D Street is now Denton Street.
Bay Way is now Bayway; its north end at Edgar Road is now the Bayway Circle (Routes 1 and 9), and Edgar Road has been rebuilt as a highway.
Washington Avenue is marked not opened; the modern Carlton Street runs near its line.
Myrtle Street north of Grier Avenue is marked not opened.
Laura Street, at the lower left edge, is marked not defined.
Two hand-picked points (Bayway / Grier Avenue, South Broad Street / Summer Street) were added where the detector found no junction.

100 ft. Bayway at the Linden line: Allen Ave, Grier Ave, Bay Way, Summer Ave, Myrtle, Morses Mill Rd, E St (Bonnett), D St (Denton), South Broad. One part; beyond Edgar Rd and the NE corner blank (Vol. 2).

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the ground between Summer Avenue and Grove Street south of South Broad Street, in the south-western part of the city, down to the Elizabeth River. South Broad Street runs along the top, with the area north of it left blank and marked "See Volume Two"; Grove Street runs down the right edge, with the ground east of it also left for Volume Two apart from the ends of Williamson, Rector and Pearl Streets. Summer Avenue runs down the left edge. Maple Avenue, Hetfield (marked not graded) and Clarkson Avenue (not graded) cross the sheet, and Garden Street runs south from South Broad Street to Clarkson Avenue, not graded south of Hetfield. The two blocks between South Broad Street and Maple Avenue and the block south of Maple are built up with frame dwellings, many two to three storeys, on narrow lots, with a boarding house and the Elizabeth Boiler Repair and Sheet Metal Works at South Broad Street and Summer Avenue. The largest works is the Dual Leathers Corporation, makers of upholstery leather, south of Maple Avenue towards Grove Street, with japanning, fitting and pressing buildings and storehouses. South of Hetfield the blocks are empty. The Elizabeth River crosses the bottom of the sheet from right to left, with an iron bridge carrying Summer Avenue; beyond it the street ends of sheets 32 and 22 are sketched without buildings, outside this part's mask.
notes: Hetfield (lettered "Green St." at Summer Avenue) is now Green Street; its junctions with Summer and Garden lie about 4 to 6 m from the modern line, so it was left out of the fit.
Summer Avenue is now Summer Street.
Rector Street, east of Grove Street, is probably the modern Nelson Avenue.
Garden Street south of Hetfield, Hetfield and Clarkson Avenue are marked not graded.
The Dual Leathers Corporation, makers of upholstery leather, occupies most of the block south of Maple Avenue at Grove Street.
The Grove Street junctions were hand-picked; the detector found no lines along Grove Street.
100 ft. Summer Ave to Grove St south of South Broad: Maple Ave, Hetfield, Clarkson Ave, Garden St; Dual Leathers Corp.; Elizabeth River at the bottom (masked). One part.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the Bayway district south of South Broad Street, between Laurel on the city line at the left and Chelsea at the right, down to Trenton Avenue. Laurel runs along the boundary with Linden Township, whose side is left blank and marked "See Volume Two"; north of Clarkson Avenue Laurel is marked not open. Myrtle Street, Bayway (80 ft wide), Richmond and Chelsea run down the sheet, with Franz Josef Avenue and Fern Place in the southern blocks. Across the sheet run South Broad Street at the top, F Street, G Street, Clarkson Avenue, McKinley, Brunswick Avenue and Trenton Avenue at the bottom. At the upper right Maple Avenue runs diagonally from Bayway, with C Street and Green Street curving away to the north-east. The Theodore Roosevelt School No. 17, with an auditorium and gymnasium, occupies the block between South Broad Street, Myrtle Street, F Street and Bayway, and a contractor's yard and a vacant club house stand near Clarkson Avenue. North of McKinley the ground is mostly empty large blocks. Between McKinley and Trenton Avenue the blocks are cut into narrow lots built with small frame dwellings and stores, many two storeys, some stuccoed on hollow tile, with a barber shop on Bayway near Trenton Avenue. Block outlines of sheets 37, 40 and 41 are sketched at the edges. The compass rose stands at the upper left beside the scale note, and the scale bar at the lower left.
notes: F Street is now Ogden Street and G Street is now Thomas Street.
Laurel is now part of Allen Street.
Brunswick Avenue east of Bayway is now Pulaski Street; the modern Brunswick Avenue between Myrtle Street and Bayway runs diagonally across the old blocks.
C Street is probably the modern Carteret Street.
Franz Josef Avenue, Chelsea and the southern blocks towards Trenton Avenue have been cleared for the New Jersey Turnpike and the Goethals Bridge approaches; no modern junction survives there.
Polonia Avenue, between Clarkson Avenue and McKinley Street, did not yet exist.
Laurel north of Clarkson Avenue is marked not open.
Theodore Roosevelt School No. 17 occupies the block south of South Broad Street between Myrtle Street and Bayway.
The strip below Trenton Avenue at the lower left is lettered Myrtle St.
100 ft. Laurel (city line) to Chelsea, South Broad to Trenton Ave: Myrtle, Bayway, Richmond, F St, G St, Clarkson, McKinley, Brunswick, Franz Josef Ave, Fern Pl; Roosevelt School 17. One part.

sheet-40-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 40, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the ground south-east of Maple Avenue and west of the Elizabeth River in the south-western part of the city. At the top, Maple Avenue, Green Street (lettered with its former name Richmond), Chetwood Street (formerly Brighton), Clarkson Avenue and Arnett Street (A Street) run diagonally from the upper left towards Summer Avenue, crossed by Britton Street and by C Street at the left edge. This upper area is the built part of the sheet: blocks 1, 2 and 4 hold rows of small two-storey frame dwellings, many of them numbered, with a plumber's shop on Maple Avenue and a group of concrete-block buildings behind it; a sewer pumping house with an underground concrete roof stands on Clarkson Avenue. Blocks 3, 5 and 6 towards Summer Avenue are laid out in lots but empty. Below the curve where the two parts of Clarkson Avenue meet, a straight grid of large empty blocks runs south to Trenton Avenue along Green, Chelsea, Brighton and Clifton Streets, crossed by Brunswick Avenue; none of it is built. The Elizabeth River crosses the right half of the sheet; Summer Avenue crosses it on an iron bridge to South Fifth Street, and the street ends of Loomis, Redcliffe and Doyle Streets on the far bank belong to sheet 32. A heavy line at the lower right separates the inset of block 12 (part 2); the compass rose and scale bar sit beside it.
notes: Green Street is lettered "Green (Richmond)" and Chetwood Street "Chetwood (Brighton)", giving their earlier names.
Arnett Street is lettered "Arnett (A St.)"; its modern line lies a few metres from the drawn one.
C Street is probably the modern Carteret Street.

Brunswick Avenue is now Pulaski Street at Clifton Street; Chelsea and Brighton in the southern grid no longer exist, and the southern blocks are now New Jersey Turnpike and Goethals Bridge approach land.
A sewer pumping house with an underground concrete roof stands on Clarkson Avenue near Britton Street.
Summer Avenue crosses the Elizabeth River on an iron bridge.
The detector misplaced Britton / Chetwood, Chetwood / Summer and Clarkson / Summer by about 40 to 50 ft; these three were hand-picked.

100 ft. Maple Ave to Trenton Ave, Green (Richmond), Chetwood (Brighton), Clarkson, Arnett (A St), Britton, Summer Ave, Clifton; Elizabeth River. Two parts: main map and an inset of block 12 (Maple/Summer/Britton/Green) behind a heavy line at lower right, drawn about 10 % larger.

sheet-40-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 40 is an inset at the lower right, set off by a heavy line, showing block 12, which lies north of the main map between Maple Avenue, Summer Avenue, Green Street and Britton Street; it would otherwise fall off the top of the sheet, where the main map leaves its place blank. The block is laid out in narrow lots running back from Summer Avenue and Britton Street, almost all of them empty; the only building is a small two-storey store at the corner of Maple Avenue and Britton Street. Water pipes are drawn along all four streets, with a fire alarm box at Maple and Summer. The ends of the neighbouring streets are sketched around it: Hetfield Street continues Green Street east of Summer Avenue, and the numbers 37, 38 and 40 mark the sheets that show the adjoining blocks. The inset appears to be drawn at the sheet's scale of 100 ft to an inch, but its spacing between Maple Avenue and Green Street is about 10 percent larger than on the main map and on sheet 38.
notes: Green is lettered "Green (Richmond)"; Hetfield Street east of Summer Avenue is now also Green Street.
Placed on only three junctions (Maple / Summer detected, Green / Summer and Britton / Green hand-picked); the first-order fit is exact and has no check.
The drawn distance from Maple Avenue to Green Street along Summer Avenue is about 405 ft, against about 370 ft on the main map of this sheet and on sheet 38.

100 ft. Maple Ave to Trenton Ave, Green (Richmond), Chetwood (Brighton), Clarkson, Arnett (A St), Britton, Summer Ave, Clifton; Elizabeth River. Two parts: main map and an inset of block 12 (Maple/Summer/Britton/Green) behind a heavy line at lower right, drawn about 10 % larger.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the southern Bayway district between Laurel on the city line at the left and Brighton at the right, from Trenton Avenue at the top down to Burlington Avenue. Myrtle, Bay Way (80 ft), Richmond and Chelsea run down the sheet; across it run Trenton Avenue, Mack, Pulaski, Edith Avenue, Woodbridge Avenue, Merchant, Long Branch Avenue, Princeton Avenue and Burlington Avenue, with Fern Place and Franz Josef Avenue stubbing in from sheet 39 and Krakow Street at the bottom. Linden Township beyond Laurel is left blank for Volume Two. The blocks north of Woodbridge Avenue, and those along Bay Way below it, are cut into narrow lots with small frame and plastered dwellings, stores and a bake house. Two railroads cross the lower half diagonally: the Central Railroad of New Jersey's Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch, and a line on a trestle 20 ft high that crosses Bay Way on a steel bridge. Between them and Richmond lies the Atlantic Chemical Works Ltd., makers of coal tar products, with a sublimating building, tar paper building, naphtha and naphthalene buildings, a cooperage, stills, cooling tanks and many storage tanks. South of the branch the works of Byron Heffernan and Co., manufacturers of coal tar and inorganic chemicals (plant not in operation), has warehouses, still houses, a dryer and a machine shop on Princeton Avenue. A scrap iron and metal yard stands near Long Branch Avenue at the left. Most blocks south of Woodbridge Avenue and east of Richmond are empty, and Chelsea and Richmond are marked closed in places. The compass rose is at the left and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Almost the whole sheet has been rebuilt for the New Jersey Turnpike, the Goethals Bridge approaches and the realigned Bayway; no modern junction lies on an old street line here (the modern Bayway / Trenton Avenue node is about 200 m from the old Bay Way / Trenton Avenue corner).

Placed by a helmert fit on two points along Trenton Avenue carried from sheets 39 and 40 (first-pass placements): old Bay Way / Trenton Avenue and Brighton / Trenton Avenue. Low confidence; at the bottom of the sheet Bay Way lies about 5 to 6 m across from where sheet 43 (also a helmert) puts it.
Works: Atlantic Chemical Works Ltd. (coal tar products) and Byron Heffernan and Co. (coal tar and inorganic chemicals, plant not in operation).
Laurel is now part of Allen Street; Chelsea and Richmond are marked closed in places.
100 ft. Laurel to Brighton, Trenton to Burlington Ave; Atlantic Chemical Works, Byron Heffernan & Co.; CRR Perth Amboy Branch. One part; no surviving junction, placed from sheets 39 and 40.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers almost entirely unbuilt ground on both sides of the Elizabeth River in the south of the city, between Brighton at the left edge and 4th Avenue at the right, and from Trenton Avenue and Baltic at the top down to Burlington Avenue and Little Smith at the bottom. West of the river a straight grid of large empty blocks is laid out along Brighton, Clifton (closed), a street marked "not named" (closed) and Trenton, Woodbridge (closed), Princeton (closed) and Burlington Avenues. East of the river the streets of the Elizabethport grid run diagonally from the river bank to 4th Avenue: Baltic, Caspian (closed), Delaware (closed), Erie (closed), Florida, Geneva, 2nd Street, Butler and Little Smith (closed), with Fifth Avenue at the top edge. The blocks are numbered but empty; the only buildings are two small ones at the top right corner. The Central Railroad of New Jersey's Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right, crossing the river on a bridge, and a branch curves off it to the north-east. Trenton Avenue crosses the river on a bridge at the top. Lot numbers in the 400s and 600s mark the street frontages. The compass rose stands beside 4th Avenue at the right and the scale bar at the bottom left.
notes: Nearly the whole sheet is now New Jersey Turnpike and interchange land; the old Erie, Florida, Geneva, 2nd and Butler Streets now end at 3rd Avenue, about 40 m beyond the right edge, and the old 4th Avenue is gone.

Placed on one detected junction (Clifton Street / Trenton Avenue), Brighton / Trenton Avenue carried from sheet 40, and a derived point stepped 750 ft down Clifton Street at the atlas scale and sheet 40's rotation; low confidence. Checked by eye: the modern South 2nd Street and the railroad fall on their drawn lines.
Woodbridge, Princeton, Caspian, Delaware, Erie and Little Smith are marked closed, as are Clifton and the unnamed street north of the railroad.
100 ft. Elizabeth River, Brighton to old 4th Ave, Trenton to Burlington/Little Smith; empty blocks, CRR. One part; placed on Clifton/Trenton, a point from sheet 40 and a derived point.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43, drawn at 50 ft to an inch (a scale of feet, not the 100 ft scale note of the neighbouring sheets), covers the industrial ground of Bayway at the south-western edge of the city, between Laurel on the city line at the left and Bay Way at the right, from the Central Railroad of New Jersey's Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch at the top down to Amboy Avenue and the match line with sheet 44 at the bottom. Princeton Avenue crosses the upper part diagonally, and Burlington Avenue and Myrtle, both marked closed, run through the works. Linden Township beyond Laurel is left blank and marked "See Volume Two". The Elizabeth Foundry Co. occupies the middle of the sheet, with a moulding and foundry building of steel frame and cement block, an engine and blower room, a pattern shop and a second steel-frame foundry with cupola and core ovens. East of it the Skinner Bros. Mfg. Co. Inc., makers of heating equipment, has a storage building, a boiler house, vacant shops and a sheet metal works with offices along Bay Way. Below, the Bayway Smelting Corporation has a hollow-tile smelting building and a babbitt smelting shed. Near Amboy Avenue stand cotton warehouses Nos. 8 and 9 and barrel warehouse No. 3 of the Bayway Terminal, referred to sheet 44, and below Amboy Avenue a carpenter shop and other buildings of the American Copper Products Corporation. Sidings of the Central Railroad's Shore Line curve through the sheet from the branch at the top towards the bottom right. Block 1, west of Myrtle and north of Princeton Avenue, is empty. The dash-dot match line A-B at the bottom marks the edge of sheet 44.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch (fitted 7.8 px/ft), unlike the 100 ft sheets around it.
Placed by a helmert fit on two street junctions along Amboy Avenue (Myrtle and Bay Way) and one rail crossing on the same street; low confidence, rotation fixed by points on one line only.
Princeton Avenue and Burlington Avenue no longer exist; Myrtle and Burlington are marked closed.
Laurel is now part of Allen Street; Bay Way is Bayway.
Works: Elizabeth Foundry Co., Skinner Bros. Mfg. Co. Inc. (heating equipment), Bayway Smelting Corporation, Bayway Terminal warehouses, American Copper Products Corporation.
50 ft (scale of feet). Laurel to Bay Way, CRR branch to Amboy Ave; Elizabeth Foundry, Skinner Bros, Bayway Smelting. One part; helmert on Amboy Ave.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44, drawn at 50 ft to an inch (a scale of feet), covers the shore of Staten Island Sound at the southern tip of the city's Bayway district, between Laurel on the city line at the left and Bay Way at the right, below the match line A-B shared with sheet 43. South Front Street crosses the sheet, and Myrtle (marked closed) runs north from it. Linden Township beyond Laurel is left blank and marked "See Volume Two". North of South Front Street the Bayway Terminal storage warehouses fill the left half: fire-proof concrete cotton warehouses Nos. 4, 6 and 11 (built 1919 and 1921), barrel warehouse No. 7, steel tanks and a pump house, with the American Copper Products Corporation (owners) and Bayway Terminal (lessee) lettered on barrel storage No. 1. To the right are the American Copper Products Corporation's copper wire mills: a rolling mill, casting shop, melting pots, stock and mixing rooms, oil tanks, a water-proofing department and a water tank, served by a siding. South of South Front Street the company's main works runs down to a plank dock on the Sound: a long fire-proof building holding the wire mill, fine wire mill, rod mill, pickling department, straining department, tinning and cable departments, with an office, a shipping building, a pipe shop and an oil house nearby. A printed note gives the plant's fire protection, pumps drawing water from Staten Island Sound. The open ground west of the works slopes to the shore, which runs diagonally across the lower left. A railroad siding and South Front Street continue beyond Bay Way at the right edge.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch (fitted 7.9 px/ft).

Only two street junctions survive (South Front Street at Myrtle Street and at Bayway); two more points were carried from sheet 43's first-pass placement at the ends of the shared match line A-B, so the fit depends on sheet 43 (itself a helmert); low confidence.
The American Copper Products Corporation's copper wire mills fill most of the sheet; the shoreline has since been filled and rebuilt.
Laurel is now part of Allen Street; Myrtle is marked closed.
50 ft. Laurel to Bay Way below match line A-B, South Front St, Staten Island Sound; Bayway Terminal, American Copper Products wire mills. One part; placed with sheet 43.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the southern end of Elizabethport between Butler Street and Staten Island Sound, from Elizabeth Avenue at the top down to 4th Avenue, with the mouth of the Elizabeth River running down the middle of the sheet. Butler, Little Smith (not opened in part), South 1st Street (First Street north of Elizabeth Avenue) and South Front Street run down the sheet; 2nd Avenue meets Butler at the left edge, and 3rd and 4th Avenues cross the western half. At the top, between South 1st and South Front Streets, stands the large plant of The Barrett Co., manufacturers of roofing and paper, with paper machines, pulp beaters, tar stills, storage buildings and its own fire pump, in operation day and night. West of it are The Thomas and Betts Co. machine shop and a row of small dwellings on Little Smith. Below lies the Organic Products and Color Co., makers of leather and textile chemicals (Apex Chemical Co. lessee), and beyond it extensive lumber piles of The Heidritter Lumber Co., which also fill the strip between the river and South Front Street, with a planing mill and sheds. A draw bridge carries South Front Street over the river. On the shore of the Sound are the New Jersey Dry Dock and Transportation Co., with shipways, a marine way, a dry dock and plate and shingle shops, the Connelly Iron Sponge and Governor Co. oxidizing works, and the New York Lubricating Oil Co. oil storage and compounding works. Railroad sidings run through the works. The large blocks 1 and 7 west of South 1st Street are almost empty.
notes: Works: The Barrett Co. (roofing and paper), The Thomas and Betts Co. machine shop, Organic Products and Color Co. (Apex Chemical Co. lessee), The Heidritter Lumber Co., New Jersey Dry Dock and Transportation Co., Connelly Iron Sponge and Governor Co., New York Lubricating Oil Co.
The east half of the sheet, the river mouth and the shore have been rebuilt; only junctions in the western streets were used.
Little Smith is marked not opened north of block 2.
Butler Street / Elizabeth Avenue was not detected (Butler is drawn slanting at the top of the sheet).

100 ft. Butler to Staten Island Sound, Elizabeth Ave to 4th Ave; Barrett Co., Heidritter Lumber, NJ Dry Dock & Transportation, Connelly Iron Sponge, NY Lubricating Oil. One part, turned (rotation -55).

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the waterfront at the southern end of the city between the Elizabeth River and Staten Island Sound, from 4th Avenue and the river at the top down to Bay Way at the bottom, and from Burlington Avenue at the left edge to the shore of the Sound at the right. South 1st Street crosses the Elizabeth River on a bridge and continues south as Amboy Avenue; Clifton, Brighton, Chelsea, Richmond and Krakow streets run across the left half between Burlington and Amboy avenues, laid out in large, mostly empty blocks, with the narrow lots of Richmond and Krakow streets only beginning to fill with small frame dwellings and sheds near Bay Way. The Public Service Electric Co. Bayway substation stands on Krakow Street. The right half, east of the Central Railroad of New Jersey line that runs down the sheet, is an oil and chemical district along South Front Street and the Sound: the New York Lubricating Oil Co., the National Rosin Oil & Size Co., the Pennsylvania & Delaware Oil Co., the Galena-Signal Oil Co. tank field, the New York Oil Storage & Transfer Co., the Cook & Swan Inc. fish oil refinery, the Borne-Scrymser Co. lubricating oil works and, at the foot of the sheet, the Bowker Chemical Co. fertilizer and heavy chemical works, each with numbered oil tanks, sidings and a printed note on its fire protection. The B. & N.Y. R.R. crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally on a trestle, drawn as a yellow band, and leaves over a steel bridge towards Staten Island. Small dwellings, tenements and shops line Bay Way at the bottom edge.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch.

Almost the whole sheet is now covered by highway interchanges (Goethals Bridge approach, Bayway) and industrial ground; Clifton, Brighton, Chelsea, Richmond, Krakow, Burlington and Little Smith have no counterpart in the modern street data.
South 1st Street north of the river and Amboy Avenue south of it are one road, as today; the modern name changes at the bridge.
The B. & N.Y. R.R. (now the Staten Island Railroad) crosses on a trestle 20 ft high; its modern line lies about 5 to 7 m from the drawn one, so its crossings were not used as control.
Bowker Chemical Co. is marked 'Admission refused, information obtained from previous survey'.
Borne-Scrymser Co. buildings are noted as fire-proof reinforced concrete with hollow tile curtain walls, built 1917.

100 ft; south waterfront between Elizabeth River and Staten Island Sound: S. 1st St bridge, Amboy Av, Bay Way, S. Front St, Clifton/Brighton/Chelsea/Richmond/Krakow (gone), oil and chemical works, B.&N.Y. trestle; one part; low confidence (4 points).

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers four blocks in the south of Elizabethport between 2nd Avenue at the top and 4th Avenue at the bottom, from Atlantic Street at the left edge to Erie Street at the right, with Baltic, Caspian and Delaware streets in between and 3rd Avenue crossing the middle. The upper half is residential: narrow lots along Atlantic, Baltic, Caspian, Delaware and Erie streets hold two-storey frame dwellings, a few flats and stores, with sheds, coops and stables in the rear yards, and the Scandinavian Lutheran Church at the corner of Atlantic Street and 2nd Avenue. A broad railroad strip between Baltic and Caspian streets carries the Central Railroad of New Jersey, Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch, which crosses 2nd and 3rd avenues on iron bridges. The lower half is industrial. The Kalbfleisch Corporation chemical works fills the block between Baltic Street and the railroad, with sulphuric and nitric acid buildings, acid chambers, a sulphur pile, a hydrochloric acid building, salt storage and a sulphate of soda plant. East of the railroad stand the closed New York Chemical Refining Co. and timber sheds, and the block between Delaware and Erie streets is taken by the Elizabethtown Gas Light Co. gas works with a gas holder of 1,000,000 cubic feet, purifiers, a boiler house and generator house. An iron trestle on concrete footings runs off the lower right corner. Between Atlantic and Baltic streets the lower block holds rag storage and pressing sheds, a junk yard and the cement block works of Owen Tobiason. The sections of Caspian Street and 4th Avenue next to the chemical works are marked closed.
notes: Caspian Street is now Lieutenant Glenn Zamorski Drive in the modern street data.
Baltic Street has no modern counterpart; the line along the railroad has been absorbed.
4th Avenue east of Atlantic is gone; no junction on the 4th Avenue row was used, so the lower half of the sheet is placed by extrapolation from the 2nd and 3rd Avenue rows.
Caspian Street south of 3rd Avenue and 4th Avenue between Caspian and Delaware are lettered 'Closed'.
The C.R.R. of N.J. Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch crosses 2nd and 3rd avenues on iron bridges.
The Kalbfleisch Corporation, manufacturers of chemicals, occupies the block between Baltic Street and the railroad south of 3rd Avenue.
Elizabethtown Gas Light Co. gas works: 'see note, sheet 48'.
New York Chemical Refining Co. is marked closed.
50 ft; 2nd to 4th Av, Atlantic, Baltic, Caspian, Delaware, Erie; Kalbfleisch chemical works, gas works, C.R.R. E.&P.A. branch; one part.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers eight blocks in the south of Elizabethport between 2nd Avenue at the top and 4th Avenue at the bottom, from Erie Street at the left edge to Butler Street at the right, with Florida Street, Geneva Street and South 2nd Street between them and 3rd Avenue across the middle. The four blocks between 2nd and 3rd avenues are built up with narrow lots of two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, some flats and stores, with stables, coops, sheds and storage buildings behind; Batnor's Garage, for 25 cars, stands on Erie Street. The block between South 2nd and Butler streets is taken by a shoe factory, the Biltwell Shoe Co. Inc. (tenants, Anna Hawkes owner), with manufacturing, finishing, stock and lasting rooms, unused boilers, and a row of vacant buildings owned by B. Frank along Butler Street. Below 3rd Avenue the corner block at Erie Street holds the Elizabethtown Gas Co. gas plant, in continuous operation, with purifying houses, engine rooms, generator houses, a relief holder of 340,000 cubic feet, a gas oil tank, a machine shop and a carpenter shop. The other three blocks between 3rd and 4th avenues are laid out in numbered lots that are almost all empty; only a small store stands on South 2nd Street. 4th Avenue runs along the bottom edge, with a scale bar between Florida and Geneva streets.
notes: The blocks between 3rd and 4th avenues, almost all empty lots in 1922, are now gone with 4th Avenue; the lower half of the sheet is placed by extrapolation from the 2nd and 3rd Avenue rows.
Elizabethtown Gas Co. gas plant, in continuous operation, at Erie Street and 3rd Avenue (continued on sheet 47).
The Biltwell Shoe Co. Inc. occupies the shoe factory at South 2nd Street and 2nd Avenue; Anna Hawkes, owner.
Batnor's Garage, capacity 25 cars, on Erie Street.
50 ft; 2nd to 4th Av, Erie, Florida, Geneva, S. 2nd, Butler; gas plant, Biltwell Shoe; empty lots below 3rd Av; one part.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers the area where Elizabeth Avenue, 1st Avenue and the Central Railroad of New Jersey meet at the south-western edge of Elizabethport, from Elizabeth Avenue at the top to 2nd Avenue at the bottom and from 4th Street and Baltic Street at the left to Erie Street at the right, with Caspian and Delaware streets running down the sheet and Merrit Avenue crossing its lower half. The C.R.R. of N.J. Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch runs down the sheet between Baltic and Caspian streets, crossing 1st Avenue at grade beside two signal towers and 2nd Avenue on an iron bridge; the Elizabeth Avenue passenger station stands in the railroad block with a ticket office and waiting rooms on either side of the tracks, joined by a tunnel. In the upper left, between 4th Street and the railroad, the corner block holds a motion picture theatre, dwellings, and the fire-proof concrete storage warehouse, store house and express buildings of George Weimar, built in 1918. Along Elizabeth Avenue east of the railroad stand dwellings and an auto sales and service garage. The open triangle where 1st Avenue meets Elizabeth Avenue at 3rd Street holds the Mack Monument. The lower right quarter is residential, with frame dwellings, a few flats and stores on narrow lots along Caspian, Delaware and Erie streets, St. Peter and Paul's Greek Catholic Church on 1st Avenue and Public School No. 11 on Erie Street at Merrit Avenue. The land west of Baltic Street in the lower left is blank (drawn on sheet 36).
notes: Caspian Street is now Lieutenant Glenn Zamorski Drive in the modern street data.
Merrit Avenue is spelled Merritt Avenue today.
Baltic Street has no modern counterpart.
Elizabeth Avenue passenger station of the C.R.R. of N.J. (Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch), with a tunnel under the tracks.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 covers eight residential blocks of southern Elizabethport between Elizabeth Avenue at the top and 2nd Avenue at the bottom, from Erie Street at the left edge to Butler Street at the right, with Florida Street, Geneva Street and South 2nd Street running down the sheet and Merrit Avenue crossing the middle. Almost every lot holds a two-storey frame dwelling, with a few three-storey flats, stores on the corners, and stables, coops and sheds in the rear yards; several houses are brick-cased or stuccoed. The institutions stand along Elizabeth Avenue: the Free Public Library between Erie and Florida streets and the Greystone Presbyterian Church, with its tower, at the corner of Florida Street. The only works are the Simon & Mendelsohn underwear factory at Erie Street and Merrit Avenue, a bakery with a hollow-tile oven on Geneva Street, and a boiler shop at Butler Street and Merrit Avenue (drawn in full on sheet 45). The block corners along Elizabeth Avenue are cut back where the avenue widens to 95 ft at the left of the sheet. Water pipes with their sizes are drawn along every street, and a scale bar sits below 2nd Avenue at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Merrit Avenue is spelled Merritt Avenue today.
Free Public Library on Elizabeth Avenue between Erie and Florida streets.
Greystone Presbyterian Church at Elizabeth Avenue and Florida Street.
Simon & Mendelsohn, underwear manufacturers, at Erie Street and Merrit Avenue.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 covers the western end of the Elizabethport grid between 7th Street at the left and 6th Street at the right, from East Jersey Street at the top down to 1st Avenue at the bottom, with Fulton, Franklin and Marshall streets and Elizabeth Avenue crossing the sheet. New Point Road cuts diagonally across the upper block from 7th Street towards East Jersey Street, leaving triangular corner lots. The blocks are lined with two- and three-storey frame dwellings, flats and stores on narrow lots, with stables, coops and sheds behind; a stuccoed hall stands at New Point Road and Fulton Street, and a repair shop and garage with buried gasoline tanks on Fulton Street near 7th Street. The largest works is the Rising Sun Brewing Co. on 7th Street between Franklin Street and Elizabeth Avenue: office and storage, a bottling department, a brew house with malt mill and clock tower, brewing, engine and ice machine rooms, a spray pond and storage buildings, with a printed note on its watchman, pumps and cisterns. Other businesses include a vacant building with a night watchman and a store house on Franklin Street at 6th Street, the Standard Welding Co. on Marshall Street, a mission, a bake house, a wet wash laundry and plumbing supplies along Elizabeth Avenue, and stores along 1st Avenue at the bottom edge. The land west of 7th Street is blank (drawn on sheets 24 and 26).
notes: Rising Sun Brewing Co. on 7th Street between Franklin Street and Elizabeth Avenue.
Standard Welding Co. on Marshall Street near 6th Street.
New Point Road crosses the upper blocks diagonally, as today.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers four long blocks of the Elizabethport grid between 6th Street at the left and 5th Street at the right, from East Jersey Street at the top down to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, with Fulton, Franklin and Marshall streets crossing the sheet. It is a dense residential district of narrow lots, almost all built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and flats, many in continuous rows, with small stores at the corners and along East Jersey Street and Elizabeth Avenue, and stables and sheds in the rear yards. Public School No. 8 fills the 6th Street end of the block between Fulton and Franklin streets, and the Evangelical Lutheran Church with its chapel stands at 6th and Franklin streets. Along Elizabeth Avenue the lots hold stores of two and three storeys, among them a bakery with ovens at 6th Street, a sausage factory, hardware and paints, and an auto sales building; a dress manufactory with an electric motor stands on Franklin Street and a carpenter and lumber shed on Fulton Street. The streets outside the blocks, beyond 6th and 5th streets, are left blank for the neighbouring sheets 51, 53, 58 and 35, and a scale bar sits below Elizabeth Avenue.
notes: Public School No. 8 between Fulton and Franklin streets at 6th Street.
Evangelical Lutheran Church and chapel at 6th and Franklin streets.
East Jersey Street is lettered 'E. Jersey'; 6th Street is 90 ft wide at East Jersey Street.
Elizabeth Avenue is lettered 80 ft wide.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 covers four long blocks of the Elizabethport grid between 5th Street at the left and 4th Street at the right, from East Jersey Street at the top down to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, with Fulton, Franklin and Marshall streets crossing the sheet. It is a dense residential and shopping district: nearly every narrow lot holds a two- or three-storey frame dwelling or flat, many brick-cased, with stores of two and three storeys along East Jersey Street and Elizabeth Avenue and on the corner lots, and stables, coops and sheds in the rear yards. Businesses include a blacksmith and a plumber near 5th Street, a laundry on 5th Street, a hardware and paints store on East Jersey Street, bakeries with ovens at East Jersey and 4th streets and at Franklin and 4th streets with a wagon shed, a carpenter shop on Franklin Street, a club house on Elizabeth Avenue, and a news distributing station on Marshall Street at 4th Street. A windmill stands in the rear of the lots behind East Jersey Street. The 1st Methodist Protestant Church, with a 50 ft tower, stands at the corner of Franklin and 4th streets. The ground beyond 5th and 4th streets is blank for the neighbouring sheets 52, 54, 59 and 36, and a scale bar sits below Elizabeth Avenue.
notes: 1st Methodist Protestant Church, with a 50 ft tower, at Franklin and 4th streets.
East Jersey Street is lettered 'E. Jersey'; Elizabeth Avenue is lettered 80 ft wide and the other streets 60 ft.
A windmill stands behind the East Jersey Street lots near 4th Street.
A buried 550 gallon gasoline tank is marked on 5th Street near East Jersey Street.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 covers four blocks of the Elizabethport grid between 4th Street at the left and 3rd Street at the right, from East Jersey Street at the top down to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, with Fulton, Franklin and Marshall streets crossing the sheet. The Central Railroad of New Jersey, Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch, runs down the sheet through the middle of the blocks, and a curved siding on a trestle 5 ft high serves a coal, wood and masons' materials yard behind East Jersey Street. The blocks are lined with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with stores at the corners and along East Jersey and 3rd streets. Businesses include a drug store and a cabinet shop with a buried gasoline tank on East Jersey Street at 4th Street, a printing shop with an electric motor, a furniture store and a Chinese laundry on 3rd Street, a cement shed, a poultry market, a blacksmith, a bottling works on 4th Street near Elizabeth Avenue, a plumber and a junk yard on Elizabeth Avenue. St. Adelbert's Roman Catholic School and St. Adelbert Convent occupy the 3rd Street end of the block between Franklin and Marshall streets. The Mack Monument appears at the lower right corner where 1st Avenue meets Elizabeth Avenue. The ground beyond 4th and 3rd streets is blank for the neighbouring sheets 53, 55, 60 and 49, and a scale bar sits below Elizabeth Avenue.
notes: C.R.R. of N.J. (Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch) crosses the sheet between 4th and 3rd streets.
St. Adelbert R.C. School and St. Adelbert Convent at 3rd Street between Franklin and Marshall streets.
Coal, wood and masons' materials yard served by a siding on a trestle off East Jersey Street.
Mack Monument at Elizabeth Avenue and 1st Avenue (lower right corner).
50 ft; 4th to 3rd St, E. Jersey to Elizabeth Av, C.R.R. branch; St. Adelbert school; one part.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 covers four blocks of the Elizabethport grid between Third Street on the left and Second Street on the right, from East Jersey Street at the top down to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, with Fulton, Franklin and Marshall Streets crossing between them. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that the numbered streets run up the page. The blocks are almost wholly residential: narrow lots of two- and three-storey frame dwellings, many with rear sheds, with stores on several corners. The largest buildings are institutional. The Polish Catholic Church, its rectory and the Polish Catholic School fill the Third Street end of the block between East Jersey and Fulton. The Old Fulton Street M.E. Church, with a tower, stands mid-block on the south side of Fulton Street, and the East Baptist Church faces Third Street at the corner of Franklin; the Boys Club of Elizabeth occupies a building on the north side of Franklin. Commercial and industrial uses are few: an auto house and service station and a small auto service building on East Jersey Street near Second, auto repairing shops at the Second Street end of the Fulton and Franklin block, the Frederick Rieke shirt factory (power and lights electric, heat steam) on the south side of Marshall Street, and a hollow concrete block garage for 35 cars with a buried gasoline tank between Marshall Street and Elizabeth Avenue. Water pipes and their sizes are drawn along every street, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Below Elizabeth Avenue the sheet shows only the ends of First Avenue, Erie Street, Florida Street, Geneva Street and South Second Street, belonging to sheet 50, and a monument at the corner of Third Street.
notes: Numbered streets are 3rd Street and 2nd Street in OpenStreetMap; South Second Street below Elizabeth Avenue meets it as 2nd Street / South 2nd Street.
Elizabeth Avenue is lettered 95 ft wide; the other streets 60 ft.
