3rd to 2nd St, East Jersey to Elizabeth Ave (Fulton, Franklin, Marshall); Polish Catholic church and school, East Baptist church; one part.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers four blocks of the Elizabethport grid between Second Street on the left and First Street on the right, from East Jersey Street at the top to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Fulton, Franklin and Marshall Streets. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page, and continues sheet 55 to the west. The interior of every block is lined with two-storey frame dwellings, while the First Street frontage is a continuous row of brick and frame stores with dwellings over, including drug stores at the corners of East Jersey and Franklin, a hardware and paints store and a furniture store. Commercial and industrial buildings stand among the houses: a moving picture theatre and the Electric Battery Works on East Jersey Street; the Fulton Specialty Co. manufacturing building (wood working) on the south side of Fulton Street, with a row of tenements behind it; the Elizabeth Iron Works Co. structural iron works on Franklin Street and a second structural iron works shop on Marshall Street; and a laundry, an auto paint shop and a machine shop and welding shop on the north side of Elizabeth Avenue. Fire House No. 4 of the fire department, with Police Precinct No. 2, Truck No. 2 and Engine No. 4, faces Elizabeth Avenue, and its apparatus is listed beneath it. Garages and auto houses of hollow tile and concrete block are scattered through the yards. Water pipes are drawn along every street. Below Elizabeth Avenue only the ends of Butler Street, Smith Street and South First Street are drawn, belonging to sheets 50 and 45.
notes: Fire House No. 4 with Police Precinct No. 2 on Elizabeth Avenue; apparatus listed on the sheet.
Elizabeth Iron Works Co. structural iron works on Franklin Street.
Fulton Specialty Co. wood-working factory on Fulton Street.
Two junctions hand-picked (2nd Street / Franklin Street, 1st Street / Elizabeth Avenue): the detector paired a street edge with a water pipe.
2nd to 1st St, East Jersey to Elizabeth Ave; Fire House No. 4, Elizabeth Iron Works; one part.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 covers the Elizabethport blocks between Seventh Street on the left and Sixth Street on the right, from Court Street at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway and Livingston Street; New Point Road cuts diagonally across the lower right from East Jersey Street to Sixth Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page. The block between Court and South Park Streets is lined with two-storey frame dwellings and a row of three-storey flats, with many empty lots. Below South Park Street the sheet becomes industrial. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along Broadway (100 ft wide) and a siding curves off it through the block to the north, past a concrete-block hay storage building. South of Broadway are the Elizabeth Sash, Door and Supply Co. (cabinet shop, wood planing, lumber sheds and lumber yards), The American Cigar Co. Factory No. 1, a stone yard, and M. Carroll's coal yard with a coal shed with track over it. Between Livingston and East Jersey Streets the Alexian Brothers' Hospital fills most of the Seventh Street end of the block, with wards, chapels, kitchens and a boiler room described in detail. In the triangle cut off by New Point Road stand the Livingston Baths, stores and the New Point Garage (blacksmith and wood shop, wagon and auto body manufacturing, machine shop). Elsewhere the blocks hold dwellings, stores and auto houses. A compass rose sits in Broadway and the scale bar below the hospital.
notes: Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks run in Broadway, drawn 100 ft wide; Broadway was left out of the control because the tracks mislead the detector.
Alexian Brothers' Hospital between Livingston and East Jersey Streets at Seventh Street.
The American Cigar Co. Factory No. 1 and the Elizabeth Sash, Door and Supply Co. between Broadway and Livingston Street.
Livingston Baths and the New Point Garage on New Point Road.
7th to 6th St, Court to East Jersey; New Point Road diagonal; CRR of NJ in Broadway; Alexian Brothers' Hospital; one part.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers the Elizabethport blocks between Sixth Street on the left and Fifth Street on the right, from Court Street at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway and Livingston Street. New Point Road enters from sheet 57 near Broadway and runs diagonally up to the right, crossing South Park Street and Court Street and leaving the sheet near Fifth Street; it cuts the blocks into irregular wedges and triangles. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page. The district is mainly residential: rows of two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, three-storey flats and corner stores, with small auto houses in the yards and a hall on Court Street. A row of dwellings lines the New Point Road front of the block below Broadway. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along Broadway, drawn 100 ft wide, with a spur curving into the block to the south. There the main works is A. Lamy & Son, designers of grate bars, with a machine shop, a pattern shop, storage, an office and a boiler for testing. Elsewhere there are a few small industrial uses: an ice house and office near Livingston Street, a hollow-tile building and garages. The Livingston to East Jersey block has houses, three-storey stores with dwellings over along East Jersey Street, and a concrete-floored moving picture theatre at its Fifth Street end. Water pipes are drawn along every street, and a compass rose sits in Broadway.
notes: Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks run in Broadway (100 ft); Broadway was left out of the control.
A. Lamy & Son, designers of grate bars, with machine and pattern shops between Broadway and Livingston Street.
New Point Road crosses the sheet diagonally; its junction with South Park Street was hand-picked and agrees with the modern road to about 1.6 m.
6th Street / Court Street and 5th Street / Court Street were hand-picked.
6th to 5th St, Court to East Jersey; New Point Road diagonal; A. Lamy & Son; one part.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 covers the Elizabethport blocks between Fifth Street on the left and Fourth Street on the right, from Court Street at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway and Livingston Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page. This is a dense residential and shopping district: the street fronts are lined with two- and three-storey frame dwellings, flats and stores with dwellings over, many of them brick-fronted on the ground floor, and the yards hold auto houses and sheds. Two synagogues stand on the Court to South Park block: the stuccoed South Park Synagogue mid-block on South Park Street and the brick Beth Israel Synagogue at the corner of Fourth Street, and on Court Street are the United Hebrew Charity Association school and assembly rooms and a dance hall. Small trades are scattered through the blocks: bakeries with ovens, a milk depot and a bottling works, a poultry shop, a carpenter shop, a bake house, a tin shop, a tailor shop and a pattern shop with electric motors. The largest works is Hickey & Schneider, manufacturers of electrical supplies, with a forge shop, iron storage and machine shops on the north side of East Jersey Street, beside a steam laundry and another bottling works. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along Broadway, drawn 100 ft wide. Water pipes with their sizes are drawn on every street, a compass rose sits on Court Street and the scale bar below East Jersey Street.
notes: South Park Synagogue and Beth Israel Synagogue on the Court to South Park block.
United Hebrew Charity Association school and assembly rooms on Court Street.
Hickey & Schneider, manufacturers of electrical supplies, on East Jersey Street.
Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks in Broadway; Broadway left out of the control.
4th Street north of Livingston Street is not used for control: 4th Street / South Park Street has no modern node and 4th Street / Court Street sits off the old line.
5th to 4th St, Court to East Jersey; two synagogues; Hickey & Schneider; one part.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 covers the Elizabethport blocks between Fourth Street on the left and Third Street on the right, from Court Street at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway and Livingston Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page. The Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs straight down the middle of the sheet across every street, and the main line in Broadway (100 ft wide) curves into it from the left, with sidings serving the yards on both sides; a small C.R.R. of N.J. station with a waiting room stands at Fourth Street and Broadway. Public School No. 5 fills the Fourth Street end of the Court to South Park block. East of the railroad are the M. E. Castles shirt and shirt waist factory, a bakery, and, south of South Park Street, a coal and building material yard with an elevator, storage of mason's supplies and a trestle, beside Fire Department Station No. 5, whose apparatus is listed. Between Broadway and Livingston Street are the Lackawanna Ice Co., with an ice house and storage of cement blocks, a lumber yard, and a bakery and paint and oil store on Third Street. The Livingston to East Jersey block holds a metal stamping and auto tire shop, a machine shop, Storey's Elizabeth, Newark and New York Express storage, Post Office Sub-Station A, a closed moving picture theatre, a lunch wagon and a fireproof garage at the railroad. The rest is two-storey dwellings and three-storey stores and flats. A compass rose sits in Broadway.
notes: Elizabethport and Perth Amboy Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet; a C.R.R. of N.J. station at Fourth Street and Broadway.
Public School No. 5 between Court and South Park Streets.
Fire Department Station No. 5 on Third Street south of South Park Street.
Post Office Sub-Station A at Third and Livingston Streets.
The modern 4th Street / Court Street node sits about 4 m off the drawn junction and was left out; 3rd Street / Court Street was hand-picked.
4th to 3rd St, Court to East Jersey; CRR Elizabethport & Perth Amboy branch; Public School No. 5, Fire Station No. 5; one part.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 covers the Elizabethport blocks between Third Street on the left and Second Street on the right, from Court Street at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway and Livingston Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page. In the upper half, Park Place runs between Court Street and Broadway, and east of it Jackson Park fills the whole block to Second Street, drawn with its radiating dashed walks around a central circle and a small comfort station; South Park Street is interrupted by the park and resumes beyond Second Street. The two blocks west of Park Place hold dwellings and stores, a wall paper store and a hall and gymnasium with bowling alleys in the basement. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along Broadway (100 ft wide), and a spur curves off it into the next block, ending at a trestle in the C. E. Pountney coal, wood and grain yard with its storage, baled hay, grain and auto sheds. In the same block are the German Presbyterian Church parish hall, the rectory and St. Nicholas Russian Orthodox Church at the Third Street end, the Elizabeth Knee Pants Co. with a tailor shop and sewing room, and the J. P. Hebendahl, Zucker & Sons Co. silver polish and machine shop. Between Livingston and East Jersey Streets stand Public School No. 1, stores and a hollow tile building at Third Street, and the Grace Episcopal Church parish hall with the Franklin A. C., Inc. bowling alleys and pool hall at Second Street.
notes: Jackson Park fills the block between Park Place and Second Street from Court Street to Broadway.
St. Nicholas Russian Orthodox Church and the German Presbyterian Church parish hall on Third Street.
C. E. Pountney coal, wood and grain yard served by a spur and trestle from the Central Railroad of New Jersey in Broadway.
Public School No. 1 between Livingston and East Jersey Streets.
Grace Episcopal Church parish hall and Franklin A. C. bowling alleys at Second and East Jersey Streets.
Broadway left out of the control because of the tracks.
3rd to 2nd St, Court to East Jersey; Park Place, Jackson Park; Public School No. 1; one part.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 covers the Elizabethport blocks between Second Street on the left and First Street on the right, from Court Street at the top to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway and Livingston Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page, and lies east of Jackson Park on sheet 61. The interior lots are almost all two-storey frame dwellings with small auto houses, while First Street is lined with two- and three-storey stores with dwellings over, among them an upholsterer, a laundry, a furniture and carpets store, drug stores and, at the corner of East Jersey Street, a bank. A trucking and storage building and a concrete-block garage stand on the south side of South Park Street, with a buried gasoline tank. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along Broadway, drawn 100 ft wide. The block between Broadway and Livingston Street is the industrial one: The Union Foundry of R. S. Christie, with a foundry, cupola, machine shop and storage, and the F. A. Williams & Sons brass foundry, with a pattern shop, furnace and shipping room, stand side by side near Second Street, and further east the Elizabeth Rescue Mission wood yard and dormitories and a vulcanizing shop face Broadway, beside a machine shop on Livingston Street. Between Livingston and East Jersey Streets are dwellings, flats, an undertaker, a carpenter shop and garages of tile and concrete block. A doctor's office stands at Second and South Park Streets. Water pipes are drawn on every street, a compass rose sits on Second Street and the scale bar below East Jersey Street.
notes: The Union Foundry (R. S. Christie) and F. A. Williams & Sons brass foundry between Broadway and Livingston Street.
Elizabeth Rescue Mission wood yard and dormitories on Broadway.
A bank at First Street and East Jersey Street.
Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks in Broadway; Broadway left out of the control.
Court Street junctions hand-picked: the detector paired a Court Street edge with the water pipe at First Street and missed Second Street.
2nd to 1st St, Court to East Jersey; Union Foundry, F. A. Williams brass foundry; one part.

sheet-63-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 63, the lower part of the page below a heavy dividing line. It covers the north-east end of the Elizabethport grid between Seventh Street on the left and Sixth Street on the right, from Court Street at the bottom edge up to Magnolia Avenue, with Trumbull Street crossing diagonally above it and Bond Street meeting Sixth Street at the upper right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the numbered streets running up the page, like the neighbouring sheet 57. The block between Court Street and Magnolia Avenue is residential: two-storey frame dwellings, a few stores with dwellings over, a row of tenements, small auto houses and a machine shop; at the corner of Seventh Street and Magnolia Avenue stands a concrete-block public garage for 30 cars with a buried gasoline tank, and a small oven building sits behind the houses. North of Magnolia Avenue the wedge between Magnolia and Trumbull Street has a store at its point and dwellings toward Sixth Street, and a block between Trumbull, Bond and Sixth Streets holds only a stuccoed hollow-tile auto house and a row of dwellings. Above Trumbull Street the area to the heavy line is mostly blank: open lots of block 4 and the outlines of the neighbouring sheets 29, 30 and 74, with a street marked closed. Water pipes are drawn along the streets, the compass rose sits beside the dividing line, and the scale bar is printed in Court Street.
notes: Magnolia Avenue is lettered 'Magnolia Av. (Wall)', giving its older name Wall Street.
Magnolia Avenue west of Trumbull Street is now part of Trumbull Street; its junction with Seventh Street was hand-picked at the modern 7th Street / Trumbull Street node (residual 1.3 m).
Sixth Street north of Court Street is East 6th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Court Street runs along the bottom edge with its south side not drawn; 7th Street / Court Street was hand-picked.
Public garage for 30 cars at Seventh Street and Magnolia Avenue.

three parts behind heavy lines: (1) 7th to 6th St, Court to Magnolia Ave (Wall), Trumbull, Bond; (2) top-left inset of block 1 on Trumbull St / Isham Pl, unplaced; (3) 2nd and 1st St, Trumbull, McKenzie Pl, Isham Pl, Singer Mfg Co ball park (helmert).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at top left: west end of block 1 between Trumbull Street and Isham Place (no street junction drawn; needs step 6b from sheet-63-3, or sheets 73/76 if they draw the block).

sheet-63-3.description: Part 3 is the upper band of sheet 63, between a heavy dividing line across the middle of the page and a heavy L-shaped line around the inset in the top left corner. It shows a separate area at the eastern end of Elizabethport, beside the Singer Manufacturing Company works: Second Street runs up the left side, First Street along the right, Trumbull Street (80 ft) crosses diagonally at the top, and McKenzie Place and Isham Place run between Second and First Streets; Isham Place is marked closed east of Second Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned like the rest of the sheet. Most of the band is the Singer Mfg. Co. ball park, with a long shed along McKenzie Place and bleachers behind a hotel at the corner of Second Street. The block between Trumbull Street, McKenzie Place and First Street holds the Singer Mfg. Co. lunch and recreation building, three-storey stores, a restaurant, a second hotel with its kitchen, and four-storey flats on First Street. West of Second Street a wedge of block 1 between Trumbull Street and Isham Place has three-storey flats and empty lots, continued in the inset at the top left of the sheet. Water pipes of 6 to 12 inches are drawn in the streets, and the outlines of the neighbouring sheets 73, 76 and 98 are lettered in the margins.
notes: Isham Place is placed as Monsignor Kemensis Place in OpenStreetMap; the 2-point fit agrees with the scale and rotation of part 1 to 0.5 percent and 1 degree, but nothing independent confirms it.
McKenzie Place has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap; the ball park is built over.
A street segment just inside the dividing line is lettered 'Second St.'.
Placed by a two-point helmert (2nd Street / Trumbull Street and 2nd Street / Monsignor Kemensis Place): low confidence.

three parts behind heavy lines: (1) 7th to 6th St, Court to Magnolia Ave (Wall), Trumbull, Bond; (2) top-left inset of block 1 on Trumbull St / Isham Pl, unplaced; (3) 2nd and 1st St, Trumbull, McKenzie Pl, Isham Pl, Singer Mfg Co ball park (helmert).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at top left: west end of block 1 between Trumbull Street and Isham Place (no street junction drawn; needs step 6b from sheet-63-3, or sheets 73/76 if they draw the block).

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 covers the north-western edge of Elizabethport between 6th Street on the left and 5th Street on the right, from the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Trumbull Street at the top down to Court Street at the bottom, with Pine Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue (marked 'Wall') crossing the sheet. It is a thinly built district. The upper third is taken up by the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which run diagonally across the top of the sheet towards Port Avenue, with sidings curving into the yard of the Heidritter Lumber Co. (coal, wood, lumber, timber), whose lumber sheds A to G and open lumber piles fill the triangle between the railroad, Trumbull Street and Pine Street; the company also has a sash, door and blind warehouse and a lumber warehouse on Pine Street at 5th Street. The block between Pine and Bond is laid out in lots but entirely empty, and a diagonal lot line crosses it and the block below. Between Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue small frame dwellings stand only at the 6th Street and 5th Street ends of the block. The block between Magnolia Avenue and Court Street is more built up, with two-storey frame dwellings, a brick-veneered dwelling, the Workmen's Circle Labor Lyceum hall, and at the 5th Street corner a garage for 30 cars with a buried 550-gallon gasoline tank and a store. New Point Road crosses the lower right corner, running diagonally from Court Street to 5th Street. Water pipes of 6, 10 and 12 inches are drawn in the streets. The blank ground at the left edge belongs to sheet 63, the right edge to sheet 65 and the area below Court Street to sheet 58; sheet 75 covers the area above the railroad.
notes: Heidritter Lumber Co. (coal, wood, lumber, timber) has its yard, lumber sheds and warehouses between the railroad and Bond Street.
The block between Pine Street and Bond Street is laid out in lots but has no buildings.
Workmen's Circle Labor Lyceum hall stands on the block between Magnolia Avenue and Court Street.
5th Street is lettered 'Fifth St.' at the top right corner and '5th St.' further down.
Pine Street between 6th and 5th Streets no longer exists; 6th Street is 'East 6th Street' in the modern reference north of Court Street.
Magnolia Avenue is lettered 'Magnolia Av. (Wall)'.
50 ft; 6th (East 6th) to 5th, Trumbull/CRR to Court; Pine, Bond, Magnolia (Wall), New Point Rd; Heidritter lumber yard; one part.

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 covers the residential blocks of Elizabethport between 5th Street on the left and 4th Street on the right, from Port Avenue at the top down to Court Street at the bottom, crossed by Pine Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue (marked 'Wall'). Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, carries the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, with a track on a trestle 10 feet high along its south side and a signal at Schiller Street. Below Port Avenue, the block at 5th Street is the yard of the Heidritter Coal & Lumber Co. (no watchman, no fire apparatus), with long lumber sheds, an office and scales on Pine Street. New Point Road, carrying 4-inch and 12-inch water pipes, runs diagonally across the sheet from 5th Street near Court Street up to Port Avenue, cutting the blocks into triangles; Schiller Street, 50 feet wide, leaves Port Avenue at the top beside a small triangular block. The rest of the sheet is closely built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and some stores, most on narrow lots numbered 400 to 463, with a few brick-veneered stores, a printing shop, a bottling works, a junk (rag) store, a club house, a carpenter shop and a restaurant. The Hungarian Presbyterian Church stands on Magnolia Avenue at New Point Road, and a large automobile shed with cement floors faces Port Avenue near 4th Street. A drug store stands at 5th Street and Court Street. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins show the edges of sheet 64 to the left, sheet 66 to the right, sheet 71 above Port Avenue and sheet 59 below Court Street.
notes: Heidritter Coal & Lumber Co. yard occupies the block between Port Avenue and Pine Street at 5th Street.
Hungarian Presbyterian Church stands on Magnolia Avenue at New Point Road.
A Central Railroad of New Jersey track runs on a trestle 10 feet high along Port Avenue.

The streets between 5th and 4th Streets north of Court Street (Pine, Bond, Magnolia, Schiller, New Point Road and Port Avenue here) are gone from the modern street network; modern 4th Street no longer runs on its drawn line.
Magnolia Avenue is lettered 'Magnolia Av. (Wall)'; 5th Street is lettered 'Fifth St.' at the top left corner.
50 ft; 5th to 4th, Port Ave to Court; Pine, Bond, Magnolia, Schiller, New Point Rd (all gone today); one part; 4th St points carried from sheet 66.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 covers the Elizabethport blocks between 4th Street on the left and 3rd Street on the right, from Port Avenue at the top down to Court Street at the bottom, crossed by Pine Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue (marked 'Wall'). Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, carries several tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, and the railroad's Elizabethport & Perth Amboy Branch runs straight down the middle of the sheet, splitting each block in two. The largest premises are the tenant, storage and manufacturing buildings of the American Grocers Society Inc. (owners) on the block between Port Avenue and Pine Street east of the branch: a row of numbered brick buildings, No. 1 to No. 15, used for grocery warehousing and packing and for manufacturing, with automatic sprinklers, a power house with a 200-horsepower engine, an auto house, a siding off Port Avenue and two water tanks of 50,000 and 100,000 gallons; a night watchman and clock and steam power are noted. The rest of the sheet is closely built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and stores on narrow lots numbered 300 to 363, with tenements, a cobbler, a plumber, a bakery with an oven, the Woodstein Bottling Works, a garage for 30 cars in a concrete-block building on Magnolia Avenue, and drug stores at 4th Street and at 3rd Street on Court Street. Many stores line 3rd Street. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins show the edges of sheet 65 to the left, sheet 67 to the right, sheet 71 above Port Avenue and sheet 60 below Court Street.
notes: American Grocers Society Inc. (owners) tenant, storage and manufacturing buildings Nos. 1 to 15 fill the block between Port Avenue and Pine Street east of the Perth Amboy branch.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey's Elizabethport & Perth Amboy Branch runs through the middle of every block on the sheet.
Woodstein Bottling Works stands on Bond Street.
A concrete-block garage for 30 cars stands on Magnolia Avenue.
Modern 4th Street does not follow its drawn line here; only junctions on 3rd Street were used as control.
50 ft; 4th to 3rd, Port Ave to Court; American Grocers Society buildings; CRR Perth Amboy branch; one part; control on 3rd St only (helmert).

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 covers the Elizabethport blocks between 3rd Street on the left and 2nd Street on the right, from Port Avenue at the top down to Court Street at the bottom, crossed by Pine Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue (marked 'Wall'), with Park Place leaving Court Street at the bottom. Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, carries the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, and a siding curves off it into the W. N. Stevenson Co. umbrella factory and warehouse on the block between Port Avenue and Pine Street, a brick building with ovens under reinforced concrete ceilings. The rest of the district is closely built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots numbered 200 to 262, and with stores along 3rd and 2nd Streets: drug stores at 3rd and Pine and at 2nd and Bond, a saloon, a lunch room, a restaurant, paint stores, a hardware and paint store with a hollow-tile storage building, a Chinese laundry, an electric motor shop and stores marked 'gutted by fire' on 2nd Street. The south block between Magnolia Avenue and Court Street holds the parish of St. Patrick's: St. Patrick's R. C. Church, of stone, with two spires 212 feet high, its rectory, St. Patrick's High School and St. Patrick's Grammar School, together with a Y.M.C.L. building and a house of the Sisters of Charity. Jackson Park is lettered beyond Court Street on the margin belonging to sheet 61. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins show the edges of sheet 66 to the left, sheet 68 to the right and sheet 73 above Port Avenue.
notes: St. Patrick's R. C. Church, with two 212-foot spires, its rectory, high school and grammar school fill the block between Magnolia Avenue and Court Street.
W. N. Stevenson Co. umbrella factory and warehouse, with a railroad siding, stands between Port Avenue and Pine Street.
Y.M.C.L. building and a Sisters of Charity house stand on the St. Patrick's block.
Stores at 2nd and Magnolia are marked 'gutted by fire'.
The 3rd Street / Port Avenue and 2nd Street / Port Avenue junctions were left out as control: modern Port Avenue does not run on the drawn line here.
50 ft; 3rd to 2nd, Port Ave to Court, Park Pl; St. Patrick's church and schools; one part.

sheet-68.description: Sheet 68 covers the Elizabethport blocks between 2nd Street on the left and 1st Street on the right, from Port Avenue at the top down to Court Street at the bottom, crossed by Pine Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue (marked 'Wall'). Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, carries the main tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, with further tracks curving away towards the yard on sheet 74 at the top. This is the commercial heart of the port district: the block between Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue at 2nd Street is filled by the M. Levy & Son department store, a large brick building with stores, apartments on the upper floors, automatic sprinklers and a 20,000-gallon water tank, and next to it a moving-picture theatre of hollow tile. 1st Street and 2nd Street are lined with brick and frame stores, and the side streets with two-storey frame dwellings, flats and tenements on narrow lots numbered 100 to 163. Other premises include a garage for 30 cars in a concrete-block building on 1st Street with a buried gasoline tank, a machine shop and an electric motor shop on Pine Street, a pool and bowling hall at 2nd Street, Russian and Turkish baths and a willow chair manufactory on Bond Street, an undertaker and a Chinese laundry on 1st Street, a paint store, plumbers, and the club house of the Young Men's T.A.B. Society on Court Street. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins show the edges of sheet 67 to the left, sheet 72 to the right, sheet 74 above Port Avenue and sheet 62 below Court Street.
notes: M. Levy & Son department store, with apartments above and automatic sprinklers, fills the corner of 2nd Street and Bond Street.
A moving-picture theatre of hollow tile stands on Bond Street beside the department store.
Young Men's T.A.B. Society club house stands on Court Street.
Russian and Turkish baths and a willow chair manufactory stand on Bond Street.
Port Avenue junctions were left out as control: they carried residuals of 4 to 5 m, so modern Port Avenue is off its drawn line here.
1st Street / Bond Street appears twice in the modern data; the node 41 m south of the drawn junction was rejected (13 m).
50 ft; 2nd to 1st, Port Ave to Court; M. Levy & Son department store; one part.

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 covers the eastern end of Elizabethport between 1st Street on the left and Front Street, with the waterfront of Staten Island Sound beyond it on the right, from Court Street at the top down to East Jersey Street at the bottom, crossed by South Park Street, Broadway (100 feet wide) and Livingston Street. The left half is a dense business district along 1st Street: brick stores, furniture stores and a furniture warehouse, a photograph gallery, a restaurant, a hat factory with steam heat and electric power, a lunch room, a grocery warehouse, the I.O.O.F. building, the Americus Hall and a dance hall, a garage for 35 cars, and the boiler shop and sheet iron works of P. L. Hughes on South Park Street, with frame dwellings and stores on lots numbered 61 to 169. Between Front Street and the water the right half is taken up by the Central Railroad of New Jersey freight yard, a fan of tracks with a freight house, freight shed, storage building and platform along Front Street, and further tracks curve across the block between Broadway and Livingston Street. On the shore stand the works of the New Jersey Concentrating Co., manufacturers of chemicals (Central R.R. of N.J. owners), with buildings for mixing ores, ore grinding and smelting. Below it a public park fronts the Sound, with a recreation pier, a boat club house and a bulkheaded shoreline. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins show the edges of sheet 62 to the left, sheet 72 above Court Street and sheet 70 below East Jersey Street.
notes: Central Railroad of New Jersey freight yard, with freight house and freight shed, fills the ground east of Front Street.
New Jersey Concentrating Co., manufacturers of chemicals, has ore mixing, grinding and smelting buildings on the shore (Central R.R. of N.J. owners).
A public park with a recreation pier and a boat club house fronts Staten Island Sound.
P. L. Hughes boiler shop and sheet iron works stands on South Park Street at Front Street.
The I.O.O.F. building stands on 1st Street between Livingston and East Jersey Streets.
Broadway / Front Street was rejected (13 m): tracks fill Broadway at Front Street; the waterfront east of Front Street has been rebuilt.
50 ft; 1st to Front and Staten Island Sound, Court to East Jersey; South Park, Broadway, Livingston; CRR freight yard, NJ Concentrating Co., public park and pier; one part.

sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 covers the south-eastern corner of Elizabethport between 1st Street on the left and Staten Island Sound on the right, from East Jersey Street at the top down to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, with Fulton Street and Marshall Street crossing the sheet and Front Street running down it beside the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey. Franklin Street ends at 1st Street on the left margin. Most of the sheet is the Moore Plant of the Bethlehem Shipbuilding Corporation Ltd., which fills the block between Fulton and Marshall Streets and spreads east of Front Street to the shore: foundries A, B and C with core shop, sand mixing, pattern shops and pattern storage, a brass foundry, casting cleaning and storage, a machine shop of fire-proof construction, a pipe forge shop, a plate and angle shop and mould loft, a plate and angle mill, forges, an electric power plant of 1,000 kW, a fire-proof office building of 1921 with a vault, a fuel oil tank and a 50,000-gallon elevated tank; a note gives its watchmen, steam pump and hydrants. On the shore the former marine ways are drawn in dashed outline, marked 'all timbers removed', with hydrants among them. At the top, beside Front Street, stand the Abrew & Cooper Inc. masons' materials yard, with a concrete block works, coal and sand sheds, and the Staten Island ferry landing with its ferry house. A Standard Oil Co. oil station stands near Front Street at Elizabeth Avenue. Frame dwellings and stores line East Jersey Street, 1st Street and the block between Marshall Street and Elizabeth Avenue, with a hotel and an auto repair shop on East Jersey Street. The margins show sheet 69 above, sheet 56 to the left and sheet 45 below.
notes: Moore Plant of the Bethlehem Shipbuilding Corporation Ltd. (foundries, machine shop, plate and angle shop, mould loft, power plant) fills most of the sheet.
The former marine ways on the shore are drawn in dashed outline with the note 'all timbers removed'.
Abrew & Cooper Inc., masons' materials, and the Staten Island ferry landing stand on the shore at East Jersey Street.
A Standard Oil Co. oil station stands near Front Street and Elizabeth Avenue.
Front Street / Fulton Street was not detected: the junction is covered by the shipyard and railroad tracks.
50 ft; 1st to the Sound, East Jersey to Elizabeth Ave; Fulton, Franklin, Marshall; Bethlehem Shipbuilding Moore Plant, Staten Island ferry; one part.

sheet-71-1.description: The main part of sheet 71 covers the ground north-east of Port Avenue between 4th Street on the left and 3rd Street on the right, from the heavy line along Port Avenue and Trumbull Street at the top down to Port Avenue again at the bottom of the sheet, where the avenue and its Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks turn across the page. Inslee Place, Clark Place and Ripley Place run from 3rd Street into the part, and New Point Road crosses its left side diagonally towards 4th Street; the Elizabethport & Perth Amboy Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs straight down the middle. Block 4, the triangle between Trumbull Street, 3rd Street and Inslee Place, is laid out but empty, and the land north of the branch is largely vacant. The right half below Inslee Place is the machine and foundry works of The A. & F. Brown Co., with a store room and bench work building, a foundry with core ovens and unused cupolas, core and sand sheds, storage, wash room and chipping sheds, a blacksmith shop, a long machine shop and shafting department, a second machine shop, a pattern shop and pattern storage, an electric power plant and a fire-proof office of 1917; a note gives its watchman and clock, a Cameron fire pump and a 40,000-gallon tank raised 80 feet, and sidings run in from Port Avenue. On Clark Place near 4th Street stand two-storey frame dwellings, saloons and an auto shed. A compass rose sits beneath the heavy line. The margins show sheet 76 beyond Trumbull Street, sheet 73 beyond 3rd Street and sheets 65 and 66 beyond Port Avenue.
notes: The A. & F. Brown Co. machine and foundry works fill most of the part east of the Perth Amboy branch.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey's Elizabethport & Perth Amboy Branch runs through the middle of the part.
Block 4 between Trumbull Street, 3rd Street and Inslee Place is drawn empty.
4th Street / New Point Road was excluded: it lay 11 m off a fit to the 3rd Street junctions, so the modern node is off the drawn line.
Control rests on three junctions along 3rd Street only (helmert); position across the part depends on them.

50 ft; two parts split by a heavy line: 1 = Port Ave to Trumbull between 4th and 3rd (Inslee, Clark, Ripley Pl; A. & F. Brown Co.), 2 = top strip, Trumbull to Port Ave at Schiller St (Swiss-American File Co.), placed from neighbours.

sheet-71-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 71 is the strip at the top of the sheet, above the heavy dividing line, covering the triangle between Trumbull Street and Port Avenue on either side of Schiller Street and up to 4th Street, with New Point Road running into it from Port Avenue. Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, carries the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey along the bottom of the part. The part is dominated by the Swiss-American File Co., whose brick manufacturing buildings, stock room, offices and electric power plant fill the block between Trumbull Street, Schiller Street and New Point Road; a note gives its night watchman and clock, steam heat, electric light and power, hydrants and hose connected to an Underwriters fire pump of 500 gallons a minute. Two-storey frame dwellings and stores on lots numbered 416 to 434 stand along Trumbull Street and Schiller Street, and a lime and cement storage shed stands near Port Avenue. The upper left of the part is blank paper lettered '75', the area belonging to sheet 75 beyond Trumbull Street, and the sheet number and title are printed there. The same rotation and scale as the main part are used; the heavy line separates this strip because it lies on the other side of Port Avenue from the main part.
notes: Swiss-American File Co. manufacturing buildings fill the block between Trumbull Street, Schiller Street and New Point Road.
Schiller Street, Trumbull Street west of 4th Street and New Point Road here are gone from the modern street network; no junction in the part survives.
Placed by two points carried from neighbours: Schiller Street at Port Avenue from sheet 65 and 4th Street at Port Avenue from sheets 66 and 71 part 1 (helmert, low confidence).

50 ft; two parts split by a heavy line: 1 = Port Ave to Trumbull between 4th and 3rd (Inslee, Clark, Ripley Pl; A. & F. Brown Co.), 2 = top strip, Trumbull to Port Ave at Schiller St (Swiss-American File Co.), placed from neighbours.

sheet-72.description: Sheet 72 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, a smaller scale than the 50-foot sheets around it, and covers the north-eastern end of Elizabethport between 1st Street on the left and Front Street, with the railroad yards and the shore of Staten Island Sound beyond it on the right, from Port Avenue at the top down to Court Street, crossed by Pine Street, Bond Street and Magnolia Avenue (marked 'Wall'). Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, carries a broad band of Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks that fan out across the upper right of the sheet and run down beside Front Street towards the freight yard on sheet 69. The block between Port Avenue and Pine Street holds a lumber and cement yard with lumber and cement storage sheds, a cement block manufactory and an office, with a row of small dwellings and stores along Pine Street. The blocks between Pine Street and Court Street are closely built with frame dwellings, flats and stores on lots numbered 37 to 91, with brick stores along 1st Street, a bake house with an oven, drug stores, undertakers, a wagon shed and a stable. East of Front Street the Moore Bros. Co. machine shop and foundry fills the block between Pine and Bond Streets, with foundry, core department and ovens, cupolas, pattern storage, a machine shop, a blacksmith shop, sand houses and casting cleaning; a note gives its watchman, heating, power and fire alarm. Further east stand the store houses of the Central R.R. of N.J., tool sheds and a carpenter shop among the tracks, and the open shore of Staten Island Sound at the lower right. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins show sheet 68 to the left, sheet 98 above Port Avenue and sheet 69 below Court Street.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch (scale note and scale bar), against 50 feet on its neighbours; the fit gives 6.59 px/ft, matching 60 ft.
The Moore Bros. Co. machine shop and foundry stands between Pine and Bond Streets east of Front Street.
Central R.R. of N.J. store houses and a broad fan of tracks fill the ground between Front Street and Staten Island Sound.
A cement block manufactory and lumber and cement storage stand between Port Avenue and Pine Street.
Five of the eight control points were hand-picked from block corners: the detector found few junctions at this scale.
Front Street / Pine Street was excluded: the detector paired a line about 12 ft off the street centre.
60 ft to an inch; 1st to Front and the Sound, Port Ave to Court; Moore Bros. Co. foundry; one part.

sheet-73.description: Sheet 73 covers four residential blocks of north-east Elizabethport between Third Street on the west and Second Street on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. From top to bottom the blocks run between Trumbull Street and Isham Place, Ripley Place, Inslee Place, Clark Place and Port Avenue. Trumbull Street, 80 feet wide, crosses the upper left corner diagonally, cutting the first block into a fan of narrow wedge-shaped lots; a hotel stands at its corner with Third Street, with a barber shop and a lunch wagon beside it. The dominant institution is the parish of St. Peter's and St. Paul's (Roman Catholic): the church with two slated spires of 125 feet, a parochial school with a hall above, a separate parochial school and the rectory occupy the middle of the blocks on both sides of Ripley Place. Benjamin Franklin Public School No. 13, a two-storey brick building heated by steam, faces Ripley Place near Third Street. The rest of the sheet is closely built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with brick stores and flats on the Second Street corners, a bakery with an oven at Second Street and Clark Place, and a stone-cutting shed on Clark Place. South of Clark Place a long lot marked as owned by Julius Finkler is largely vacant, crossed by a curving siding. Port Avenue, 100 feet wide, runs along the bottom of the sheet carrying the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: Isham Place is now Monsignor Kemensis Place.
Port Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide with the Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks in it; today's right-of-way is about 70 feet and its junctions were left out of the control.
St. Peter's and St. Paul's Roman Catholic church, parochial schools and rectory.
Benjamin Franklin Public School No. 13 on Ripley Place.
Earlier edition sheet number 90 printed under the sheet number.
50 ft. 3rd to 2nd St, Trumbull St/Isham Pl (Monsignor Kemensis) to Port Av; St Peter and St Paul RC church and schools, PS 13. One part. Port Av left out.

sheet-74.description: Sheet 74 continues sheet 73 one block further east in north-east Elizabethport, covering the blocks between Second Street on the west and First Street on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The cross streets are, from top to bottom, Isham Place, Ripley Place, Inslee Place and Clark Place, with Port Avenue and the four-track main line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey along the bottom edge; a fan of sidings and a signal tower curve off the main line towards the Singer works at the lower right. Isham Place is marked closed east of the middle of the sheet, and the whole block between it and Ripley Place east of the halfway point is open ground labelled Singer Manufacturing Company Athletic Grounds. Trumbull Street clips the upper right corner diagonally. The western half of the sheet is closely built: long rows of three-storey frame flats and brick-veneered row houses on Ripley Place, two-storey dwellings on Inslee and Clark Places, and brick stores and flats on the Second Street corners, including a pool and bowling hall with a skylit roof, a saloon and a concrete-block garage. Commercial and small industrial uses include a washing machine factory with an electric motor, two bakeries with ovens and wagon sheds, and a hay, feed and coal yard with a hay shed and storage building between Clark Place and the railroad. The eastern half, toward First Street, is mostly platted but vacant lots. A signal tower stands at Second Street and Port Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in every street.
notes: Isham Place is now Monsignor Kemensis Place; it is marked closed east of the middle of the sheet.
Port Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide with the Central Railroad of New Jersey main line; its junctions were left out of the control (today's right-of-way is narrower).
Slater Drive, which meets First Street today between Isham and Ripley Places, is not on the sheet.
Earlier edition sheet number 91 printed under the sheet number.
50 ft. 2nd to 1st St, Isham to Clark Pl, Port Av and CRR main line; Singer athletic grounds. One part.

sheet-75.description: Sheet 75 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the planned but largely unbuilt grid north-east of Trumbull Street in the Elizabethport district, between Sixth Street on the west and Fourth Street on the east, with north toward the upper left. The cross streets Laura, Olive, Emma, Flora, Anna, Bond and York run across the sheet; most of them, and Sixth Street, are marked not opened, and the blocks (numbered 1 to 18) are empty outlines. Humboldt Avenue, 80 feet wide, crosses the upper half diagonally and meets Schiller Street near the compass rose; Schiller Street runs north-east along the right edge, lined with a row of two-storey dwellings that continue onto sheet 76. The Air Reduction Sales Company's experimental laboratories occupy the blocks between Flora and Bond Streets east of Fifth Street, with several laboratory buildings, hose and hydrant equipment, a storage shed and an office; a siding curves into them from the yard. The lower third of the sheet is the yard of the Central Railroad of New Jersey: dozens of parallel tracks between York and Trumbull Streets, long covered platforms and freight sheds with hydrants, an office, a signal tower, a supply house and the main line curving away to the north-east. A small group of brick and frame buildings stands at Trumbull Street near Schiller Street. Trumbull Street, 80 feet wide, runs along the bottom edge, with Pine Street and Port Avenue leaving it toward sheets 64 and 71.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.
Most streets on the sheet are marked not opened; the planned grid north of York Street was never built as drawn and the area is now industrial land beside the New Jersey Turnpike.
Dowd Avenue follows the line of old Humboldt Avenue; its junction with Schiller Street is the only modern junction inside the sheet.
Modern York Street does not lie on the line of the York Street drawn here.
Air Reduction Sales Company experimental laboratories.
Central Railroad of New Jersey yard with freight platforms and a signal tower.
Placed from three hand-picked points (Sixth and Fourth Streets at Trumbull Street, Dowd Avenue at Schiller Street); no check point.
Earlier edition sheet numbers 109 and 117 printed under the sheet number.
100 ft. Planned grid Laura..York St mostly not opened, Air Reduction labs, CRR yard; Trumbull St bottom. One part; placed by 3 hand picks.

sheet-76.description: Sheet 76 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and continues the planned grid north-east of Trumbull Street from sheet 75 eastward, between Fourth Street on the west and Second Street on the east, with Third Street down the middle and north toward the upper left. Laura, Olive, Emma, Flora, Anna, Bond and York Streets cross the sheet; nearly all are marked not opened and the blocks, numbered 1 to 18, are empty outlines. At the left edge Schiller Street runs north-east from Humboldt Avenue with a row of two-storey dwellings and a hall on its east side, continuing the row on sheet 75. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet twice: its main line runs straight across the lower part, and a branch curves up from the south-west through the blocks toward the top of the sheet. Between the main line and Trumbull Street, near Fourth Street, stand the passenger depot with its platforms, a signal tower, supply houses, and a short row of brick and frame stores and a lunch room facing Trumbull Street. The large blocks east of Third Street between Bond and York Streets carry the note that the Central Railroad of New Jersey repair shops stand there but admission to survey was refused in 1922 on account of a strike, so they are left blank. The block between the main line and Trumbull Street east of Third Street belongs to the Singer Manufacturing Company, drawn at owner's risk from plans, with a storage building with a raised floor. Trumbull Street, 80 feet wide, runs along the bottom, with Third Street, Isham Place and McKenzie Place leaving it toward sheets 71, 73 and 63.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.

Most streets are marked not opened; the grid was never built as drawn and the area is now the Jersey Gardens and New Jersey Turnpike area. Veterans Memorial Drive runs roughly on the line of Third Street north of Trumbull Street.
Central Railroad of New Jersey repair shops: admission to survey refused in 1922 on account of a strike; the blocks are left blank.
Singer Manufacturing Company block drawn at owner's risk from plans.
Placed by a helmert fit along Trumbull Street only (Fourth, Third and Second Streets); position across Trumbull Street and rotation rest on that one street.
Earlier edition sheet numbers 89, 93 and 109 printed under the sheet number.
100 ft. 4th to 2nd St north of Trumbull, CRR repair shops not surveyed (strike), Singer block, CRR passenger depot. One part; helmert along Trumbull.

sheet-77.description: Sheet 77 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers a residential district in the north-east of Elizabeth between Pennsylvania Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad embankment on the west and Adams Avenue on the east, from Fairmount Avenue at the top to Anna Street at the bottom, with north toward the upper left. Walnut Street, Jefferson Avenue, Madison Avenue and Monroe Avenue run down the sheet and Julia and Mary Streets cross it. The blocks are filled with detached two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, many stuccoed or plastered, with private garages behind. Jefferson Park occupies the whole block between Mary and Anna Streets west of Madison Avenue. Institutions include Public School No. 6 with a separate row of class rooms on Adams Avenue, the Madison Avenue Presbyterian Church above Fairmount Avenue, the Park Methodist Episcopal Church with its Sunday school on Madison Avenue, the Ardmore boarding house, and the Fire Department's Engine Company No. 6 on Pennsylvania Avenue. Industry is confined to the railroad side: the Fairmount Testing Laboratory (metal testing) on Fairmount Avenue beside the tracks, the Geo. A. Shipman Company planing mill with lumber storage off Walnut Street, and a small experimental machine shop on Madison Avenue. The Pennsylvania Railroad's four-track main line runs down the left of the sheet on an embankment; Mary Street passes under it at an iron bridge to Whitehead Place. Meadow Street cuts diagonally across the lower right corner toward Flora Street, and Linden Street leaves Anna Street at the bottom.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.
Mary Street passes under the Pennsylvania Railroad at an iron bridge.
Public School No. 6; Madison Avenue Presbyterian Church; Park Methodist Episcopal Church; Engine Company No. 6.
Fairmount Testing Laboratory and Geo. A. Shipman Company planing mill.
Whitehead Place is spelled Whithead Place in OpenStreetMap.
Earlier edition sheet numbers 35, 36, 44, 45, 46, 98, 104, 105 and 106 printed under the sheet number.
100 ft. Fairmount Av to Anna St, Pennsylvania Av to Adams Av; Jefferson Park, PS 6, Engine Co 6. One part.

sheet-78.description: Sheet 78 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers part of the north-east of Elizabeth east of Adams Avenue, from Fairmount Avenue at the top to Anna Street at the bottom and from Adams Avenue on the west to Henry Street on the east, with north toward the upper left. Meadow Street runs diagonally down the left half of the sheet, joined at the top by the short Jackson Avenue; Catherine Street and Spring Street run down the sheet, and Augusta, Julia, Laura, Mary, Olive, Emma and Flora Streets cross it. The western and southern blocks are densely built with two-storey frame dwellings in rows of narrow lots, with brick or stuccoed stores on the corners, a pool room, a barber, a cobbler, a hardware store with a gasoline tank, and private garages. Notable buildings are the Westminster Hope Memorial Church, plastered, with a belfry, on Olive Street, the Art Novelty Company works with wind power on Mary Street, a machine shop with power and lights on Flora Street, a motion picture theatre at Spring and Flora Streets, a second machine shop on Laura Street and a junk yard on Fairmount Avenue. The north-eastern quarter, between Augusta Street and Laura Street east of Spring Street, is almost empty: large blocks crossed by the dashed line of Port Avenue, marked closed, and Laura Street east of Spring marked not open. Small triangular blocks (13, 14) lie where Meadow Street meets Mary Street and Adams Avenue.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.
The diagonal stretch of Meadow Street below Julia Street is now part of Jackson Avenue; the name Meadow Street survives only for the stretch near Fairmount Avenue.
Port Avenue is marked closed across the north-east quarter; Laura Street east of Spring Street is marked not open.
Spring Street was left out of the control: the OpenStreetMap junctions lie 16 to 21 m from the drawn street (no parcel gap there to correct them).
Westminster Hope Memorial Church; Art Novelty Company; motion picture theatre at Spring and Flora Streets.
Earlier edition sheet numbers 28, 46, 48, 61, 98, 103 and 106 printed under the sheet number.
100 ft. Adams Av to Henry St, Fairmount Av to Anna St; Meadow St diagonal; Westminster Hope Memorial Church. One part; Spring St left out.

sheet-79.description: Sheet 79 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the north end of the Jefferson, Madison, Monroe and Adams Avenue grid in north-east Elizabeth, from Fanny Street at the top to the blocks just above Fairmount Avenue at the bottom, with the Pennsylvania Railroad main line and Pennsylvania Avenue along the left side and north toward the upper left. North Avenue and Louisa Street cross the sheet; Prospect Place runs from Pennsylvania Avenue under the railroad to Jefferson Avenue, and Walnut Street, marked not opened, runs beside the tracks. North Park fills the large block between Fanny Street and North Avenue west of Jefferson Avenue, unbuilt. The Pennsylvania Railroad's North Elizabeth station stands beside the tracks at North Avenue. The blocks east of Jefferson Avenue carry rows of two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, densest along North Avenue, Louisa Street and the avenues south of Louisa, where the streets bend to a different angle. Institutions are the Madison-Monroe Public School between Fanny Street and North Avenue and the Blessed Sacrament Roman Catholic Church on North Avenue between Jefferson and Madison Avenues. There are cement-floored public garages for 12 and 25 cars with buried gasoline tanks on Monroe Avenue and below Louisa Street, and a store house, but no industry. Much of the land north of North Avenue and along Pennsylvania Avenue is still open lots, and the ruins of a fire are noted at Fanny Street and Madison Avenue.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.
Prospect Place is now Hand Place.
Walnut Street beside the Pennsylvania Railroad is marked not opened.
Pennsylvania Railroad North Elizabeth station; Madison-Monroe Public School; Blessed Sacrament Roman Catholic Church.
No control below Louisa Street; the lowest third of the sheet is placed by extrapolation of the fit.

100 ft. Fanny St to below Louisa, PRR to Adams Av; North Park, Madison-Monroe PS, Blessed Sacrament RC. One part.

sheet-80.description: Sheet 80 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the north-eastern edge of built-up Elizabeth between Adams Avenue on the west and Henry Street on the east, from Fanny Street at the top to Fairmount Avenue at the bottom, with north toward the upper left. Jackson Avenue, Van Buren Avenue, Spring Street and Meadow Street run down the sheet and North Avenue and Louisa Street cross it. The western half is a residential grid of narrow lots, still largely unbuilt north of North Avenue, with rows of two-storey frame dwellings along North Avenue, Louisa Street and the avenues, a few brick stores, an auto repair shop with a buried gasoline tank, and poultry houses. Below Louisa Street the streets bend: Meadow Street runs diagonally from Spring Street down to Fairmount Avenue and the blocks between Adams and Jackson Avenues are skewed. The eastern half is industrial. The Smidth Machine and Tool Company occupies a long machine shop with raised roofs and storage on a block north of North Avenue beside Henry Street. The Copper Plate Sheet and Tube Company's fire-proof reinforced concrete plant, built in 1914, stands on a siding along an unnamed street. The largest works is Hitchings and Company, greenhouse manufacturers, with the Burnham Boiler Corporation as tenant: erecting, boiler and pipe shops, a foundry, wood-working and machine shops, pipe storage, a coal shed and a water tower with a 135,000-gallon reservoir, on a siding north of Meadow Lane. South of Meadow Lane, also called the Driftway, a large open block holds the small buildings of the Prior Chemical Corporation soap works. Two streets east of Spring Street are marked not named, and Henry Street above North Avenue is marked closed.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.
Van Buren Avenue is Vanburen Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Spring Street was left out of the control: the OpenStreetMap junctions lie about 6 m or more from the drawn street (see also sheet 78).
Henry Street north of North Avenue is marked closed; two streets east of Spring Street are marked not named.
Hitchings and Company greenhouse works (Burnham Boiler Corporation tenant); Smidth Machine and Tool Company; Copper Plate Sheet and Tube Company, built 1914; Prior Chemical Corporation soap works.
No control east of Meadow Street: the industrial east half is placed by extrapolation of the fit.
Earlier edition sheet numbers 105, 114, 118 and 127 printed under the sheet number.
100 ft. Fanny St to Fairmount Av, Adams Av to Henry St; Hitchings & Co, Smidth Machine, Copper Plate Sheet & Tube, Prior Chemical. One part; 4 hand picks.

sheet-81-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 81, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, covering the northern tip of the Jefferson, Madison, Monroe, Adams and Jackson Avenue grid between Fanny Street at the bottom and Virginia Street near the top, with Walnut Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks along the left edge. Alina Street crosses the middle of the sheet. Above Virginia Street the part is cut off by a heavy line running along a dash-dot city line; beyond the line, toward the upper right, Humboldt Avenue crosses diagonally past triangular blocks, Neck Lane runs diagonally from Virginia Street toward Jackson Avenue, and Newark Avenue, 100 feet wide, ends against the heavy line near the scale note. The ground is almost entirely platted but empty: blocks 4 to 20 are divided into narrow lots with only a handful of two-storey frame dwellings, mostly near Fanny Street and along Madison and Monroe Avenues, a laundry and a coop near Newark Avenue, a small auto body works on Adams Avenue, and a lumber shed. Several lot lines cross the blocks diagonally, following older property boundaries. North Park is lettered along the bottom edge below Fanny Street. The area to the upper right is marked as the site of proposed sheet 95, and unnamed streets run along the top.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch.
Neck Lane is drawn about 35 feet wide against 56 to 66 feet today and was left out of the control (residuals 3 to 5 m).
Humboldt Avenue here is not the Humboldt Avenue of sheets 75 and 76; no modern street was matched to it.
Area to the upper right marked for proposed sheet 95, not in the atlas.
Earlier edition sheet number 118 printed under the sheet number.
100 ft. Fanny St to Virginia St, Walnut to Jackson Av; heavy city-line boundary; part 2 = blocks on Virginia St between Sheridan and Sherman Avs, drawn turned and displaced above the line. Two parts.

sheet-81-2.description: Part 2 is the upper left corner of sheet 81, above the heavy line drawn along the dash-dot city line lettered 'See Volume 2', drawn at 100 feet to an inch but turned about eight degrees from the main map. It shows three blocks on Virginia Street between Sheridan Avenue on the left and Sherman Avenue on the right, at the northern edge of Elizabeth: block 3 north of Virginia Street, block 1 south of it, and part of block 2 east of Sherman Avenue reaching toward Newark Avenue. All three blocks are empty outlines divided by a few long lot lines, with no buildings drawn. Street widths of 60 and 70 feet are lettered. Another dash-dot city line runs along the top edge, also lettered 'See Volume 2', and the neighbouring sheet numbers 87 and 88 are printed on the blocks.
notes: Placed from two junctions only (Sheridan and Sherman Avenues at Virginia Street), as a helmert fit; low confidence.
Travers Avenue, which crosses Virginia Street today between Sheridan and Sherman Avenues, is not drawn.
Drawn at a rotation of about -37 degrees against -29 for the main part of the sheet.
100 ft. Fanny St to Virginia St, Walnut to Jackson Av; heavy city-line boundary; part 2 = blocks on Virginia St between Sheridan and Sherman Avs, drawn turned and displaced above the line. Two parts.

sheet-82.description: Sheet 82, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-eastern edge of the city between the North End and the Newark city line, from the streets west of Jackson Avenue to Henry Street at the right, and from the top of the sheet down to Fanny Street. Jackson Avenue, Van Buren Avenue and Spring Street run up the sheet; Virginia Street and Alina Street cross it, and Neck Lane runs diagonally from Jackson Avenue to Spring Street, crossing the Alina and Van Buren junction. Most of the sheet is a laid-out but unbuilt grid of 60 ft streets, many marked 'Not Named', with numbered blocks and no buildings; the area north of Virginia Street is entirely empty. The City of Elizabeth Isolation Hospital stands in blocks 5 and 7 between Van Buren Avenue and Spring Street: two stuccoed pest houses, a diphtheria ward and a scarlet fever ward joined by a passageway, and a disinfecting house, reached by a dashed roadway. East of Spring Street, Humboldt Avenue runs diagonally past the City of Elizabeth Poor Farm, with its men's and women's wards, laundry and kitchen, storage and corn crib. Drift Road to Great Island leaves the lower right of the grid, and Meadow Street meets Fanny Street at the bottom. The only ordinary housing is along Fanny Street and in blocks 11, 12 and 16 at the lower left, with small frame dwellings, sheds and a junk yard. Water pipes run in Jackson Avenue, Van Buren Avenue, Spring Street, Neck Lane and Fanny Street. Proposed sheets 93 and 95 adjoin at the right and top.
notes: Van Buren Avenue is 'Vanburen Avenue' in OpenStreetMap.
Most of the grid north of Alina Street and east of Spring Street was never built as drawn; the area now lies under Newark Liberty International Airport and its approach roads.
Humboldt Avenue, Henry Street and the unnamed streets have no modern counterpart in the reference data.
City of Elizabeth Isolation Hospital and City of Elizabeth Poor Farm.
Neck Lane is drawn about 40 ft wide, against about 60 ft for its modern right-of-way.
Meadow Street on this sheet is not the modern Meadow Street, which meets Spring Street about 400 m further south.
100 ft; Jackson, Van Buren, Spring, Alina, Neck Lane, Fanny, Humboldt Ave; Isolation Hospital and Poor Farm; mostly an empty planned grid; one part.

sheet-83.description: Sheet 83, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-western corner of the city at the Hillside Township line, between Salem Avenue at the top and the Elizabeth River at the bottom, in the North End residential district. Westminster Avenue, Union Avenue and Irvington Avenue cross the sheet from left to right; Aberdeen Road, Dewitt Road and Scotland Road run up from Salem Avenue and Westminster Avenue, Westminster Terrace joins Westminster and Union Avenues at the left, and Parker Road runs from Union Avenue down to the river at the right. The dash-dot city line crosses the lower left diagonally, with Hillside Township lettered beyond it. Housing is confined to the upper half: large frame dwellings, several stuccoed, with private automobile houses, on deep lots along Salem Avenue, Scotland Road and both sides of Westminster Avenue, and a short row of dwellings on Parker Road. The Janet Memorial Elizabeth Orphan Asylum, a brick building with steam heat and electric light, stands in block 2 between Scotland Road and Salem Avenue. Blocks 5 and 6, between Union Avenue, Irvington Avenue and the river, are laid out but empty. The Elizabeth River crosses the bottom edge, marked 'See Volume Two'. Water pipes run in Salem, Westminster and Irvington Avenues, Scotland Road and Parker Road. A compass rose and the scale bar fill the open ground at the lower left.
notes: Westminster Terrace (lettered 'Wesminster Ter.') is Malden Terrace in OpenStreetMap.
Parker Road is drawn curving east just south of Union Avenue; the modern road meets Union Avenue at two points, and neither junction was used.

sheet-84.description: Sheet 84, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the residential North End around North Broad Street, between Salem Avenue at the top, Prince Street and Magnolia Street at the right, and the Elizabeth River at the bottom. North Broad Street runs diagonally down the upper right, with Newark Avenue, Whitehead Place and Mary Street meeting it; Westminster Avenue and Union Avenue run parallel to it across the middle, and Irvington Avenue below them. Pingry Place joins Salem and Westminster Avenues, Parker Road crosses from the left edge to North Broad Street, and Rosewood, Elmwood and Oakwood Places run between Union and Irvington Avenues; Union Court is a short lane off Union Avenue in block 8. Prince Street runs from North Broad Street down to Irvington Avenue, and Irvington Place leads to a bridge over the river at the bottom. Most blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings, many stuccoed, with private garages. Institutions include the Pingry Private School for Boys in block 4 off Westminster Avenue, the Church of the Immaculate Conception with its rectory on Union Avenue, and the First Baptist Church at Union Avenue and Prince Street. In block 8 near Irvington Avenue stand the stables of the Borden Milk Co. and Fire Department Engine Company No. 7. A group of brick buildings stands at the North Broad Street end of Westminster Avenue. Blocks 9 and much of the lower left, toward the river, are empty. Water pipes are drawn in nearly every street.
notes: Whitehead Place is 'Whithead Place' in OpenStreetMap; it is drawn as a short stub, and its junction with North Broad Street fits 4.6 m off.
Magnolia Street is Magnolia Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Pingry Private School for Boys, Church of the Immaculate Conception, First Baptist Church.

sheet-85.description: Sheet 85, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the northern end of North Broad Street at the Hillside Township line, in the North End residential district. North Broad Street runs diagonally down the sheet from Wilder Street at the top left to Waverly Place at the bottom right. North Avenue crosses it, running up from Salem Avenue at the left and on east to Hazard Place; Stanton Avenue and Cross Avenue run up from North Avenue, with Stanley Terrace between them, and Clinton Place and Waverly Place run east from North Broad Street to Hazard Place. Below North Avenue, Aberdeen Road and Dewitt Road run from Salem Avenue to North Broad Street, and Scotland Road leaves Salem Avenue at the bottom. Roanoke Avenue, marked 'Not Open' in its lower part, runs parallel to North Broad Street at the left, and the dash-dot city line with Hillside Township beyond it runs down the left edge. The district is one of large detached frame and stuccoed dwellings with private garages on generous lots, many still empty. In block 2, on the west side of North Broad Street, stand the Benedictine Academy with its class rooms and the Sisters' house, and a large stone and brick dwelling; Portable School Houses of Public School No. 18 stand at the top of block 4 near Cross Avenue. Large parts of blocks 1, 2 and 3 are open ground. Water pipes, including a 12 in. main in North Broad Street and a 10 in. main in North Avenue, are drawn in most streets.
notes: Wilder Street is lettered 'Wilder (Fanny)', giving its former name.
Roanoke Avenue is marked 'Not Open' south of block 2.
Benedictine Academy and Sisters' house; Portable School Houses, Public School No. 18.

sheet-86-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 86, the main map, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the North End between North Avenue at the top and Fairmount Avenue near the bottom, from North Broad Street and Salem Avenue at the lower left to Pennsylvania Avenue at the right. Newark Avenue runs down the middle of the part, slightly off the vertical, and Pennsylvania Avenue parallels it at the right; North Broad Street crosses the lower left diagonally, with Salem Avenue beside it. Between North Avenue and Waverly Place, Hazard Place runs down to Clinton Place; Clinton Place continues east of Newark Avenue as a closed street, and Waverly Place runs from North Broad Street to Newark Avenue. Short stubs of Cross Avenue and Kilsyth Road meet North Avenue at the top, Prospect Place leaves Pennsylvania Avenue at the right, and Pingry Place appears at the bottom edge. Most lots hold detached frame dwellings with private garages, set closely along Hazard Place, Clinton Place, Waverly Place and Newark Avenue and more loosely elsewhere; the lower left between Salem Avenue and North Broad Street is largely open. A small brick silk weaving shop with electric motor power stands on North Avenue at the top right, and contractors' shops with an office stand in block 4 between Newark and Pennsylvania Avenues. Water pipes, including a 10 in. main in North Avenue, North Broad Street and Fairmount Avenue, are drawn in most streets. A heavy line cuts off the upper left corner of the sheet, which holds part 2, an inset of a separate block.
notes: Clinton Place east of Newark Avenue is marked '(Closed)'.
A silk weaving shop stands at 1210-1212 North Avenue; contractors' shops in block 4.
The junctions of Newark Avenue with North Avenue and of Hazard Place with Clinton Place fit 10 m or more off the modern nodes and were left out; North Avenue is cut by the top edge.
Junctions on North Broad Street fit 4 to 5 m off, perhaps from later widening.
100 ft; 2 parts: main (North Ave to Fairmount, North Broad to Pennsylvania), and a boxed upper-left inset of North Broad / Newark / Pennsylvania at Whitehead Pl.

sheet-86-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 86 is an inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale of 100 ft to an inch. It shows a separate block further south on North Broad Street: Newark Avenue running down the left edge into North Broad Street, Pennsylvania Avenue parallel to it, and Whitehead Place crossing between them at the bottom of the inset. The block between North Broad Street and Pennsylvania Avenue (block 8 of the sheet) is lined along North Broad Street with detached frame dwellings, one with a two-storey porch, and has a few small dwellings on Pennsylvania Avenue; the rest of the block is open. Block 1, east of Pennsylvania Avenue, holds only a short row of dwellings near Whitehead Place, and block 5 below Whitehead Place is empty. Water pipes, 10 in. in North Broad Street and Pennsylvania Avenue and 6 in. in Newark Avenue, are drawn. The inset adjoins sheet 77 to the right and sheet 84 to the left according to its edge numbers.
notes: Whitehead Place is 'Whithead Place' in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-87-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 87, the main map, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the northern tip of the city at the Newark line, between North Broad Street at the left and Sheridan Avenue at the right, from the cemeteries at the top down to Wilder Street. The Lower Road to Newark runs diagonally across the upper left beside Evergreen Cemetery, and a heavy line along it marks the edge of the area covered in Volume Two and the City of Newark; above it lies the Benai Jeschuram Cemetery with its caretaker's dwelling, green house and potting house. Below, a planned grid fills the middle of the sheet: Stanton Avenue, Cross Avenue, Grosvenor Place and Sheridan Avenue run down the sheet, crossed by Virginia Street, Hamilton Street, Fremont Place, Garfield Place and Alina Street, with a stub of Kilsyth Road at the right. Blocks 5 to 8 and 10 are divided into narrow numbered lots, nearly all still empty; a few dwellings stand on Virginia Street and near Grosvenor Place. Along North Broad Street, which runs down the left edge with King Street joining from the west and the Hillside Township line beside it, stand detached dwellings, St. Catherine's School (Roman Catholic) with its class rooms, and the Elizabeth Town Country Club with its club house, which occupies most of block 4. Thomas Jardine & Son, stone cutters, have a yard on the Lower Road at North Broad Street. Detached dwellings line the eastern part of Wilder Street at the lower right. A small area of the sheet beyond the heavy line at the upper left is drawn as a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Wilder Street is lettered 'Wilder (Fanny)'.
Grosvenor Place is the northern part of modern Kilsyth Road; only a short stub is lettered 'Kilsyth Rd.'.
Wilder Street continues east of Stanton Avenue along the bottom right (house numbers 1931 to 1939); that part is now Durant Street.
The Cross Avenue junctions with Hamilton Street, Fremont Place and Garfield Place were left out: the detector paired lot lines there (8 to 11 m off).
Elizabeth Town Country Club; St. Catherine's School (R.C.); Thomas Jardine & Son, stone cutters.

sheet-88.description: Sheet 88, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-eastern corner of the city against the Newark line and the Pennsylvania Railroad, from Cross Avenue at the left to Walnut Street beyond the tracks at the right, and from the Newark line at the top down to North Avenue. Cross Avenue, Kilsyth Road, Sheridan Avenue, Park Place and Sherman Avenue run down the left half, crossed by Alina Street and Wilder Street, with Grosvenor Place and Stanley Terrace meeting Cross Avenue at the edge; Newark Avenue runs diagonally from the top down to North Avenue. West of Newark Avenue the blocks below Wilder Street are filled with small detached frame dwellings, and a row of brick dwellings and a hall stand on Park Place; above Wilder Street, blocks 1 and 5 along Park Place and Sherman Avenue are laid out in narrow empty lots. East of Newark Avenue the whole of block 6 is taken by the Durant Motor Co. of New Jersey, built in 1922: a long fireproof concrete building with test building, stock and finished car storage, body shop and trimming, a machine shop and shipping department, a coal house, sheet metal works along North Avenue, an incline and a 100,000 gallon steel water tank, with sidings from the Pennsylvania Railroad. At the top right, in the City of Newark, stand the American Gas Accumulator Co. works and the Stanwood Rubber Co. The railroad tracks run down the right side, with Walnut Street, marked not opened, and Fanny Street beyond them. Water pipes run in most streets.
notes: Wilder Street, lettered 'Wilder (Fanny)', is Durant Street in OpenStreetMap on this sheet.
Park Place is Travers Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
