sheet-89.description: Sheet 89, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers part of the largely unbuilt planned grid in the north-east of the city, between Henry Street at the left edge and the railroad right-of-way at the right, from Fairmount Avenue at the top to Anna Street at the bottom. Fairmount Avenue, Augusta, Julia, Laura, Olive, Emma, Flora and Anna Streets cross the sheet at even spacing, Division Street runs down the middle, and Port Avenue cuts diagonally across blocks 9 to 12 from Henry Street towards Division Street. East of Division Street the cross streets are marked not opened, and blocks 1 to 8 and 11, 13, 15 and 16 are entirely empty. Building is confined to the lower left: small two-storey frame dwellings along Henry Street between Olive and Anna Streets, a row of dwellings on the north side of Anna Street (some brick or hollow tile and stuccoed), a few dwellings facing Port Avenue in block 9, a second-hand lumber yard and a junk shop in block 14, and a milk house and patent stone building in block 12. A dashed line crosses the lower right of the sheet diagonally. Water pipes are drawn only in Henry, Flora and Anna Streets.
notes: Most of the grid east of Division Street is marked 'Not Opened'.
Port Avenue has no counterpart in the modern reference data.
All control is in the lower half of the sheet (Henry Street and Anna and Flora Streets at Division Street); the empty upper half is placed by extrapolation.
In OpenStreetMap the junction of Henry Street lettered Julia Street lies where this sheet draws Laura Street, so it was not used.

sheet-90.description: Sheet 90, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, continues eastward the planned grid of sheet 89 in the north-east of the city, and shows no buildings at all. Fairmount Avenue, Augusta, Julia, Laura, Olive, Emma, Flora and Anna Streets cross the sheet from left to right at even spacing; 7th Street runs down the middle and 6th Street along the right edge, and Humboldt Avenue cuts diagonally across the top right from Fairmount Avenue towards 6th Street. Almost every street is marked not opened, and Port Avenue appears only as a short dashed stub at the lower left. Blocks 1 to 16 are drawn as empty outlines without lot lines. A dash-dot match line lettered A at the top and B at the bottom runs down the left part of the sheet, matching the same line on sheet 89; west of it the sheet repeats the eastern ends of the blocks of sheet 89. Proposed sheet 92 adjoins at the top, proposed sheet 97 at the right, sheet 75 at the lower right and sheets 29 and 30 at the bottom.
notes: The whole sheet is a planned, unbuilt grid; the streets east of Division Street have no counterpart in the modern reference data (the area is now rebuilt around Routes 1 and 9).

sheet-91.description: Sheet 91, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the open north-eastern edge of the city above the planned grid of sheet 89, between Henry Street at the left and the edge of the sheet beyond Division Street, from Fanny Street at the top down to Fairmount Avenue. North Avenue and Meadow Lane, also called the Driftway, cross the sheet; Division Street runs down the middle, Humboldt Avenue cuts diagonally across the upper part, and Louisa Street and two cross streets marked 'Not Named' complete the grid. Almost every street is marked not graded or not opened, and most blocks are empty. Two railroad lines, a branch and its sidings, curve across the upper half from the lower left to the top. In block 4, beside a siding at Henry Street, stands the Smidth-Lewis Foundry Inc., a gray metal foundry with pattern storage, office and coke oven. In block 12 stand the scattered, mostly vacant buildings of the Lowenstein Radio Co. chemical works, marked closed and dismantled. In block 13, between Meadow Lane and Fairmount Avenue, are the rendering plant, poultry house and dwelling of I. Schonwalter, and across Division Street the small rendering plant of Fred Glaser. A few dwellings and sheds stand west of Henry Street, which is marked closed between North Avenue and Meadow Lane and jogs east where it crosses Fairmount Avenue.
notes: Most streets are marked 'Not Graded' or 'Not Opened'; two are lettered 'Not Named'. The grid was never built as drawn; the area is now rebuilt around Routes 1 and 9 and the airport.
Smidth-Lewis Foundry Inc.; Lowenstein Radio Co. chemical works (closed and dismantled); I. Schonwalter and Fred Glaser rendering plants.

sheet-98.description: Sheet 98, drawn at 200 ft to an inch, the smallest scale in the volume, covers the Elizabethport waterfront north of Trumbull Street, where Newark Bay meets the Staten Island Sound. Most of the sheet is taken by the works of The Singer Manufacturing Company, a triangle bounded by Trumbull Street and First Street at the left, the Central Railroad of New Jersey main line along its north side and the shore of the Sound on the east. Its long main building, divided into numbered sections, runs along Trumbull Street, with the First Street building at a right angle; within the grounds stand foundries numbers 1 to 7, a new foundry, the forging department, hardening and annealing departments, japanning and ornamenting department, pattern storage, a power house with coal pockets, the ordnance building, box shop, rolling mill, annealing building, shipping building, storage buildings, machine storage, a locomotive house and a lumber yard, all served by a dense network of sidings. The Diehl Manufacturing Company occupies buildings at the south end. The Singer works is marked 'own risk', 'admission refused' and 'survey as shown from plans'. South of the works lies the Central Railroad of New Jersey car yard, marked 'admission to property refused 1922 on account of strike', and at the bottom the railroad and Port Avenue run to the shore past Front Street. At the left, a strip at the same scale shows the unbuilt blocks between 2nd and 1st Streets crossed by Laura, Olive, Emma, Flora, Anna, Bond and York Streets, all not opened, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey repair shops; McKenzie, Isham, Ripley, Inslee and Clark Places leave First Street to the west.
notes: Scale 200 ft to an inch (fitted 1.98 px/ft).

The shoreline has since been filled; the whole works area is now rebuilt.
